opportunities.title: 0x Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for 0x, the open-source settlement layer for permissionless exchange, covering the 0x Settler contracts, the swap and gasless APIs and the Matcha website, hosted on Immunefi.

The program page shows status 'Live Since 30 July 2024', last updated 14 July 2026, with a maximum reward of $1,000,000. A critical smart-contract finding — running under primacy of impact — pays 10% of the funds directly affected, floored at $100,000; only direct theft of user funds **at rest** is eligible for the full $1,000,000, with every other critical capped at $500,000. High smart-contract findings pay $35,000-$100,000 and medium a flat $5,000. The web/app table pays $15,000-$50,000 for critical, a flat $10,000 for high and a flat $1,000 for medium. Temporary-freeze rewards double per additional 24 hours frozen, up to the high cap.

The KYC terms are unusually concrete: a W-9 for US reporters or W-8BEN otherwise — and a researcher who declines KYC still receives 70% of the earned reward, a published fallback few programs offer. The program's own scope text lists twenty supported mainnet chains, most of them Ethereum and its L2 family.

fundingDetails.severityScheme: Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System V2.3

opportunities.summary: Rolling bug bounty for the 0x settlement layer and APIs on Immunefi, paying up to $1,000,000 for a critical finding.
opportunities.eligibility: KYC is requested for full payout — a W-9 (US) or W-8BEN (non-US) with full name, date of birth or citizenship, address and tax identification number; declining KYC reduces the payout to 70% of the earned reward. Reporters must not be on the OFAC SDN list, and official contributors, employees and auditors are ineligible. Critical smart-contract findings run under primacy of impact.
opportunities.prerequisites: A proof of concept is required at every published severity on both asset classes.
opportunities.additionalReferences: In scope: 6 assets — the 0x Settler smart contracts and the DEX meta-aggregator, plus the Matcha website, the swap API and the gasless API. The program's scope text names twenty supported mainnet chains: Ethereum and its L2 family (Base, Optimism, Arbitrum, Scroll, Linea, Mantle, Unichain, Ink, Abstract, World Chain, HyperEVM) plus Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Chain, Monad, Berachain, Fantom Sonic, Tempo and Plasma. Only direct theft of user funds at rest is eligible for the full $1,000,000 critical maximum; other criticals cap at $500,000. Critical repeatable attacks on unpausable contracts are rewarded on cumulative impact. Rewards are denominated in USD and paid in USDC on Ethereum. The program follows the Immunefi Standard. Programme page last updated 2026-07-14. Programme page: https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/0x/information/

opportunities.title: 1inch Aqua Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Bounty on the source of 1inch's Aqua intent-based swap contracts, part of the wider 1inch DEX aggregation protocol. The 32 in-scope assets are all repository paths — the Aqua, swap-vm and solidity-utils source trees — not deployed addresses.

**Pre-mainnet: only base amounts are payable.** The programme states: "As Aqua is not yet deployed on mainnet with actual user funds, all severity levels have a base reward amount. At its discretion, 1inch may decide to provide a reward up to the maximum of each respective severity level. However, any amount higher than the base reward amount is not guaranteed… By default, only the base reward amount is provided and is what security researchers should expect. Once Aqua is deployed to mainnet with live user funds, this section will be reviewed and updated to reflect production reward amounts." The $100,000 on this record is therefore the programme's published ceiling, not an amount a researcher should expect today (added 2026-08-13).

The program page states 'Live Since 11 June 2026' — the date this record carries as `postedAt` — and was live with the bounty open-ended when this record was written on 2026-08-11, with a maximum reward of $100,000; 1inch also runs separate Web, Business and Wallet bounty tracks, so this record covers the Aqua contracts only.

opportunities.title: Aave Grants
opportunities.description:
**This program has been sunset and is no longer accepting or reviewing new grant applications.**

Aave Grants DAO (AGD) was approved by the Aave DAO in May 2021 as a community grants program funded through the Aave DAO governance process — effectively a sub-DAO of the Aave DAO — with a group of Reviewers empowered to decide which proposals to fund. It funded contributors across eight categories: applications and integrations; code audits; committees & DAOs serving the Aave ecosystem; community (marketing and educational); developer tooling; events/hackathons/sponsorships; protocol development; and other. Early AGD grantees included Chaos Labs and TokenLogic, both of which later became Aave DAO service providers.

**Money.** AGD published one cumulative total for itself, in its September 2023 continuation proposal: "Since its inception in May 2021, AGD has awarded $4,852,753 across 249 grants", restated word for word in the Snapshot proposal that carried it. That is the last figure AGD ever published — it kept awarding into August 2024 but never posted the final overview it promised, and the January 2025 retrospective gives only "over 250 teams were supported" — so `allocated` here is committed-to-date as of September 2023, not a closing total.

The $500,000 ceiling is the founding proposal's own tiering: "Rapid grants: <$100k … Community grants: $100k-$500k … Contributors can also seek grants over $500k but they will not go through the committee. They will have to be posted on Aave's governance forum and approved through an on-chain vote." $500k is where this program ended and a DAO vote began. No later renewal restates or revokes the tiering, and aavegrants.org itself publishes no range.

**No `budget`, because AGD never had one envelope.** Aave funded it in five successive tranches, each sized in the proposal that granted it: $1M over two quarters at launch in May 2021; $2M for three months from December 2021; $3M per quarter for six months from May 2022; and $3.25M — $1.625M per quarter — for six months from January 2023. Any single one of them would understate the program and would sit oddly next to an allocated figure larger than it.

**Wind-down timeline:**
- August 2024 — "Update from Aave Grants: Winding Down AGD 1.0 and What's Next" announced that operations would be wound down and the team disbanded.
- January 2025 — "Reflecting on AGD's Journey and Next Steps" confirmed the wind-down, noting that as new service providers emerged their scope increasingly overlapped with AGD's broad funding mandate.
- February 2025 — an ARFC to return the remaining AGD treasury (321,768.10 GHO, 259,221.75 OP, 2,275.81 AAVE, 7,281.89 USDT, 6,738.05 USDC, 5,243.26 SAFE, 478.61 DAI) to the Aave DAO collectors passed Snapshot with 723.7K votes.
- 15 July 2026 — in response to a direct forum question asking whether the program was still active, Aave service provider TokenLogic replied: "You are correct that Aave Grants DAO has been sunset, and as part of that process, it is no longer accepting or reviewing new grant applications. As such, we wouldn't recommend preparing a submission through the AGD funding process."

The aavegrants.org site and its application form are still reachable and still carry the old rolling-applications copy, but they are stale: the site's news feed has not been updated since 2021 and the intake is not being reviewed. Prospective contributors are directed to engage the Aave DAO governance forum instead.

**Dating this record.** Aave published no announcement date for AGD, so `postedAt` is an archival bound rather than an announcement: the grants site was publicly visible by 11 May 2021, the first capture of aavegrants.org. The founding forum thread carries the corroborating update — "UPDATE – May 28, 2021: The proposal was ratified on-chain earlier this month, the grants DAO has been funded and we've started receiving applications."

opportunities.title: Aave V4 Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for **Aave V4** — the protocol's new Hub-and-Spoke architecture, where a Liquidity Hub is the canonical accounting layer and governance-permissioned Spokes implement asset-specific supply and borrow logic — hosted on Sherlock. It is a separate program from the long-running Aave v2/v3 bounty on Immunefi, which this corpus carries as its own record; the two cover different codebases and publish different tables.

The Sherlock listing shows the program live since 29 July 2026, with a $2,500,000 maximum. The tier arithmetic is published: a critical pays 10% of the funds directly affected at submission time, floored at $100,000 and capped at $2,500,000, with an absolute minimum of $10,000 at risk for a finding to classify as critical at all; a high pays up to 100% of the funds affected within $10,000-$25,000; medium ($5,000-$10,000) and low ($1,000-$5,000) carry their own published minimums. Rewards are paid in USD-pegged stablecoins, and the program names bonus considerations — report quality, a provided fix, novel attack vectors, multi-component findings — on top of the table.

Chains in scope are Ethereum and Avalanche, with all in-scope deployments maintained in the aave-address-book repository. Privileged roles (the Aave DAO and governance-approved executors) are trusted, only whitelisted standard ERC-20s are assumed, and Spokes are governance-permissioned and therefore trusted — a malicious Spoke is explicitly out of scope.

opportunities.summary: Rolling bug bounty for Aave V4's Hub-and-Spoke codebase on Sherlock, paying up to $2,500,000 for a critical finding.
opportunities.eligibility: Reports go exclusively through the Sherlock platform. Known issues, findings from previous audits pending fixes, issues requiring privileged access, and third-party dependency issues are ineligible. Testing on public mainnet deployments is prohibited — local environments or testnets only — as are social engineering, denial of service, and attempts on Aave infrastructure. Critical and High submissions carry a 250 deposit.
opportunities.prerequisites: A coded proof of concept with instructions to run it is required with every report. Where the team can pause or upgrade against an exploit, potential damage is assessed over a 1-hour exploit period. Vulnerabilities must not be disclosed publicly until verified, fixed and cleared for disclosure by the Aave team.
opportunities.additionalReferences: In scope: the Aave V4 codebase on Ethereum and Avalanche, deployments tracked in https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-address-book/ (AaveV4Ethereum.sol, AaveV4Avalanche.sol). Out of scope: third-party oracle data (Chainlink feeds are assumed correct), known and previously audited issues pending fixes, blockchain-level issues, third-party libraries, theoretical findings without a PoC, privileged-access issues, economic issues without direct fund loss, and one-block DOS unless the functionality is clearly time-sensitive. Rewards are denominated in USD and paid in USD-pegged stablecoins. opportunities.title: Alchemix Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling smart-contract bug bounty for Alchemix, the self-repaying-loan protocol, covering the Alchemix v3 contracts, hosted on Immunefi — a fresh 2026 listing, live since 26 February 2026, distinct from the protocol's earlier Immunefi program.

The program page shows last updated 10 July 2026, with a maximum reward of $150,000 for a critical finding, calculated as 10% of the funds directly affected with a $20,000 floor. High findings pay $5,000-$20,000, medium a flat $3,000 and low a flat $1,000. One reading note: the high-tier calculation text mentions a range reaching $35,000 while capping at "the maximum high reward", which the tier table sets at $20,000 — the cap governs, and the record keeps the table. Temporary-freeze rewards double per additional 24 hours frozen, up to the high cap.

The program adheres to primacy of impact for critical, high, medium and low smart-contract findings, and gates participation by researcher level: only reporters at Immunefi's Intermediate level or higher are reviewed, a published triage-bandwidth decision. Rewards are paid in USDC on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Optimism.

opportunities.title: Alchemy x Arbitrum Grant
opportunities.description:
Alchemy's Arbitrum Grant Fund is a $10,000,000 USD program of Alchemy development-platform credits for teams building or migrating to Arbitrum Orbit rollups. Awards are up to $500,000 USD per team, granted as credits applied directly to Alchemy's development platform rather than as cash, and are accompanied by co-marketing with Arbitrum and Alchemy.

As of 2026-08-11 the program page still shows **$1,000,000 remaining of the $10M total grant**, so the pool is not exhausted and applications are still being accepted. Awards are made first-come, first-served on a rolling basis with no published deadline. Applications are submitted through the contact form at alchemy.com/arbitrum-grant-contact, which asks for name, email, optional Telegram, company name and website, a description of the project, the team's current web3 infrastructure providers, and the biggest resource Alchemy can help provide.

The program is listed on the Arbitrum Foundation's own grants index as Active and 'Managed by Alchemy'.

Applications opened on 26 November 2024 — "On Nov. 26, Alchemy … opened applications for a $10 million grant program" for Arbitrum Orbit teams — and alchemy.com/arbitrum-grant was first archived the following day.

opportunities.title: ArbiFuel (Gas Fee Sponsorship Program)
opportunities.description:
ArbiFuel is the Arbitrum Foundation's Gas Fee Sponsorship Program, launched 29 May 2025, to help early-stage teams ship faster, test freely and onboard users without worrying about gas costs. Selected projects get sponsorship of **up to 1,000,000 free transactions in their first year** following the start of the gas sponsorship, **capped at $10,000 USD in credits per team**. The cap is quoted in US dollars and is delivered as sponsorship credit rather than a cash grant.

Sponsorship is initially powered by Pimlico's ERC-20 Paymasters, with plans to expand to other paymasters based on project needs, so end users do not need ETH to transact in the sponsored application. The program is framed around Arbitrum's push toward native smart-account support following upgrades such as Pectra and EIP-7702.

As of 2026-08-11 the Arbitrum Foundation's grants index lists ArbiFuel as Active, 'Managed by The Arbitrum Foundation', with a live 'Apply now' button; the Airtable intake form returns HTTP 200. No deadline or window is published — intake is rolling.

ArbiFuel also asks teams to educate their communities about being on Arbitrum and the availability of gasless transactions; the Foundation states that community education and awareness can strengthen an application.

operatingOrganizations.description: The Arbitrum Foundation stewards the Arbitrum ecosystem and administers its grant and builder programs, including ArbiFuel, the Arbitrum Audit Program and the Trailblazer grant programs.

opportunities.title: Arbitrum Audit Program
opportunities.description:
The Arbitrum Audit Program (formally the Arbitrum Audit Subsidy Program) subsidised third-party smart contract audits for projects building in the Arbitrum ecosystem. It was funded by an ArbitrumDAO vote that requested 30,000,000 ARB from the treasury to be converted into a **$10,000,000 USD** audit budget plus $60,000 USD for the elected technical expert, with all unused ARB and USDC returned to the DAO at the end of the program. The subsidy is therefore USD-denominated even though the DAO appropriation and some auditor payments are made in ARB.

The program launched on 1 August 2025 and, per the DAO proposal, ran "an on-going open application for 1 year" or until funds were exhausted. As of 2026-08-11 the Tally intake form (tally.so/r/3xzEzv?program=aap) returns "This form is now closed — the form can't receive new submissions at this moment", so the application window has ended. The Arbitrum Foundation's grants index at arbitrum.foundation/grants still shows the program as "Active" with an "Apply now" button; that listing is stale relative to the live form.

Application process: an open standardised form collecting team information, project overview and evidence of product-market fit, stage of development and timeline to mainnet, audit scope (lines of code and languages), desired completion date, preferred auditor and requested audit budget. The Arbitrum Audit Committee — chaired by the Arbitrum Foundation, with Offchain Labs, a DAO-elected technical expert (Gustavo Grieco), and the ArbitrumDAO OpCo — reviewed applications on a rolling basis against technical maturity, team experience, likelihood of success, reasonable scope and Arbitrum-first commitment. Approved projects were then matched with one of the 12 approved audit firms (OpenZeppelin, Certora, Nethermind, Trail of Bits, Ackee Blockchain Security, Oak Security, Hexens, Decurity, Pashov Audit Group, OXORIO, Cyfrin, Guardian), and the project negotiated and paid a portion of the audit itself. Subsidies were paid only after the audit completed, disbursed by the Arbitrum Foundation directly to the auditor.

No per-project subsidy cap was ever published. The DAO proposal only used a planning assumption of "~$100k subsidy per project" to size the $10M budget; it is not a published maximum award.

Program results to date: Transparency Report #3 (covering 1 Feb – 30 Apr 2026) records 258 applications received across the first three quarters (81 in Q1, 69 in Q2, 108 in Q3), approximately $1.12 million committed for approved audits since launch, total commitments expected to reach roughly $2 million including audits in progress, and 297 vulnerabilities found (8 critical, 31 high) across 21,882 lines of code reviewed.

sponsoringOrganizations.description: The Arbitrum DAO approved the Arbitrum Audit Program and appropriated 30,000,000 ARB from the treasury to fund it; unused ARB and USDC return to the DAO when the program ends.

opportunities.eligibility: Applicants had to have auditable smart contract code (e.g. Solidity or Stylus) — infrastructure outside smart contracts was not subsidised. Eligible were early-stage projects yet to launch, projects with a significant code upgrade, projects already operational on Arbitrum that could demonstrate strong product-market fit or committed ecosystem alignment, and projects migrating from another blockchain to Arbitrum. Only new code, or code that had undergone significant modification, qualified. Projects must launch in the Arbitrum ecosystem (Arbitrum One, Nova, or their own Arbitrum chain). Audited code must remain exclusive to Arbitrum for a fixed period, written into the legal agreement; breaching exclusivity obligates the project to repay the full subsidy to the DAO via the Arbitrum Foundation and may lead to legal recourse and/or a DAO proposal banning the project from future DAO-funded initiatives. Having taken venture capital or other grants did not disqualify a team, but total funds raised was weighed by the committee. This is a subsidy, not full funding — the project pays a negotiated portion of the audit cost itself.
opportunities.prerequisites: The standardised application collected: team information (names, background, notable investors); project information (overview and the problem solved, evidence or argument for product-market fit, stage of development and timeline to mainnet); audit coverage (scope of audit, lines of code and languages, desired completion date); and subsidy information (preferred auditor, optional, and the audit budget requested). Approved grantees additionally commit to publishing growth reports to the DAO at 2, 4 and 6 months after launching on Arbitrum, covering metrics such as TVL, protocol fees generated, integrations with other Arbitrum protocols and asset utilisation.

opportunities.title: Arbitrum DDA — Dev Tooling on One and Stylus
opportunities.description:
The Developer Tooling domain of the Arbitrum DAO's Delegated Domain Allocation (DDA) program, administered on Questbook. An elected domain allocator owns the domain budget, publishes its priorities and decides each award.

The domain page frames scope as four buckets. "Back to basics": essential infrastructure for asset visualisation and network interaction — e.g. an RPC built on Alchemy infrastructure, or translation of successful projects' documentation into Mandarin, Japanese, Spanish and French — plus foundations that let dApps and protocols run their own metrics systems, on the explicit view that "Total Value Locked (TVL) may not be the most appropriate metric". "Bring something cool from another chain to Arbitrum": toolkits and SDKs that make Lens-, Farcaster- or Push-style applications buildable on Arbitrum, including better documentation and MVPs for B2B SaaS-shaped functionality. "Addressing the current challenges of Arbitrum": centralization, ecosystem development and security — documentation to help build sequencers, developer SDKs for dApps "we've never heard of", and scanners that surface and improve vulnerabilities in deployed contracts. "DevRel": developer-first projects that streamline communication between developers and ecosystem stakeholders.

Worked examples the allocator publishes: IDEs for Arbitrum's chains (editor, debugger, compiler, deployer, or Arbitrum support added to existing products); SDKs and libraries for interacting with Arbitrum's smart-contract platform plus testing, deployment and monitoring tooling; testing and debugging frameworks across environments; monitoring and analytics tools covering gas usage, transaction times and user engagement; documentation and tutorial portals covering Arbitrum's API; and community forums and support channels for Arbitrum developers. Projects that lower the barrier for new developers — tutorials, articles, boilerplate, starter projects — are explicitly in scope.

Evaluation: "Proposals in this domain are typically reviewed directly by the domain allocator. Depending on the proposal content, the domain allocator may consult with allocator(s) in relevant domain(s) and may invite other allocator(s) to provide additional review." The rubric is five items each scored 0–5: Team experience; Novelty and quality of the idea; Relevance to our ecosystem; Completeness of the plan; Feasibility of goals and timeline. "Proposals that score highly in the evaluation rubric are more likely to be funded, but there is no minimum threshold number of points for funding and no threshold that guarantees funding. Grant decisions are heavily influenced by the evaluation rubric but also take into consideration the balancing of project areas."

Disbursement is milestone-gated: "All milestones are required to be filled in disbursements following the following disbursement schedule (template): Compound Milestone Tranches - Alcancía.pdf". While the domain was taking proposals it read them as they arrived, with no round deadline.

**Submissions are closed.** The program's official Season 3 thread on forum.arbitrum.foundation (topic 28753) carries the program manager's announcement of 2026-03-17: "The active phase of the program is now complete … As originally planned, submissions are now officially closed. Over the past year, we received more than 1,200 applications". The program then moved to what its own reports call a "low capacity phase" — "a phase lasting until Fall in which we just review the milestones of the approved projects and support the builders" — in which the domain allocators review and disburse milestones for already-approved projects and no new proposals are taken. The latest post in that thread, the bi-monthly report of 2026-07-22, gives the program's state across all five domains: 1,262 proposals submitted, 190 approved, 76 completed, $5.3M of $6.75M allocated (78%) and $3.4M disbursed (64%).

**No application deadline is recorded.** The program published no closing date in advance — the intake simply ended when the active phase did, announced after the fact on 2026-03-17 — so this record carries no deadline rather than a date the funder never set. The `applicationUrl` is still arbitrum.questbook.app because that is the address the DAO published for this program and where the approved proposals continue to be administered, not because new proposals are accepted there.

**Go-live.** The DDA program "went live on the 5th of October" 2023 with $800k across four domains, of which this is one; Questbook's Phase 2 continuation request on the Arbitrum forum is what dates it. Both original domains in this corpus carry that same go-live as `postedAt`, because the four domains opened together and none of them was announced separately.

**No per-domain budget is recorded.** The "Status Live" and "Available $132k" this record used to carry were read off arbitrumhub.io, a third-party aggregator still showing the domain's Season 1/2 state, and no live source replaces them. The places checked are the arbitrumhub.io domain page (still "Status Live", still "Available $132k", still naming the Season 1/2 allocator); arbitrum.questbook.app, the DAO's actual intake, which is a JavaScript application serving no figures to fetch; and the DAO's own threads on forum.arbitrum.foundation. Topic 27584, the Season 3 RFC, sizes the earlier seasons — Season 1 at "$250,000 per domain, totaling $1 million" with a "soft cap of $25,000 per project", Season 2 "expanded funding to $1,000,000 per domain" — and topic 28753, the Season 3 official thread, reports Season 3 only in program-wide terms ($5.3M of $6.75M allocated across five domains). Neither publishes a Season 3 figure for this domain on its own, so the record carries no `fundingInfo`, and no allocator is named.

**A correction to this record's earlier evidence trail.** An earlier reading of this record cited topics 27584 and 27909 alone and concluded the domain was still taking proposals. It was not: topic 27909 is the December 2024 election and application thread, it is closed with no post since 2025-02-02, and it evidences only that the domain existed in Season 3. The thread that carries the intake's actual state is topic 28753, which was not consulted then and is quoted above. Topic 27909 remains the source of the Season 3 domain name used in the title — "Dev Tooling on One and Stylus"; "Dev Tooling on One and Nova" was the Season 1/2 name, and is what this record's identifier was minted from.

**Program naming.** "Delegated Domain Allocation (DDA)" is the Season 1/2 name, kept here because it is what this record's identifier and title were minted from. From Season 3 the DAO's own threads call the program the "Arbitrum D.A.O. (Domain Allocator Offerings) Grant Program".

The Education, Community Growth and Events domain of the Arbitrum DAO's Delegated Domain Allocation (DDA) program, administered on Questbook. The elected domain allocator is reachable through the domain's Discord invite.

The allocator states its posture plainly: "We recognize that communities and the educational realm play an essential role in the growth of an ecosystem… However, we're also aware that this domain is one of the most challenging to evaluate its real impact or the quality of its content. It's vital for us to adopt a critical approach to ensure funds are allocated to initiatives that genuinely have a positive impact on Arbitrum."

Explicit exclusions: "In the educational branch, we won't back sensationalist materials or those about airdrops, ARB token quotations, or fleeting news. Our mission is to promote consistent, long-term educational content." On events: "we won't support two consecutive events from one region or the same country - this is obviously subject to demand", and content value is prioritised "rather than purely promotional strategies".

opportunities.title: Arbitrum Gaming Ventures (AGV)
opportunities.description:
**Wound down by DAO vote.** On 24 June 2026 a proposal was posted to the Arbitrum forum seeking "DAO approval for AGV to cease forward investment activity and return surplus capital to the DAO treasury for redeployment", recording that "AGV has already ceased making new investments; its remaining activities will be limited to portfolio management, information transfer, and the orderly completion of the wind-down process." It passed, and on 7 July 2026 the Arbitrum Foundation confirmed it had returned the 86.18M ARB it held on AGV's behalf to the DAO treasury — part of roughly 143.7M ARB in total, the balance being what remained inside AGV. The expression-of-interest form below was still reachable when this record was written on 2026-08-11, and the Foundation's grants index still listed the program, but new investment has ended; the 225M ARB below is what the DAO backed the program with, not what is left to deploy.

Arbitrum Gaming Ventures (AGV) is the ArbitrumDAO's gaming and consumer venture initiative — the renamed successor to the Gaming Catalyst Program (GCP). The old GCP domain thegamingcatalyst.com now redirects to arbitrumgamingventures.com, confirming the rebrand. The Arbitrum Foundation states AGV is 'Backed by 225M ARB from the ArbitrumDAO'; the figure is a native token quantity, so this record's currency is ARB rather than USD.

AGV describes itself as investing in 'teams creating exceptional experiences at the intersection of blockchain gaming, entertainment, and culture'. It 'deploys investment and grant funding to proven publishers and rising indies, using flexible deal structures such as grants, co-investments, equity, or token models to meet entrepreneurs where they are'. Support extends beyond capital to user-acquisition and scaling capital, strategic partnerships and go-to-market help, for teams ranging from AAA studios to indie creators. Its published thesis pillars are Funding Breakthroughs (projects with breakout potential, retentive user experiences and novel distribution strategies), Arbitrum Everywhere, and Bet on Talent, Big or Small.

Governance and operations: AGV is run by an operating team (Partners, a General Manager, a Venture Associate, a Grants Program Lead, a General Counsel and a Content and Communications Lead) overseen by an elected AGV Council including an Investment Committee member and an Arbitrum Foundation observer. Council seats run on a calendar-year term with nominations in October, voting in November and transition in December. The program's official start date was 1 January 2025. Its H2 2025 transparency report records the thesis broadening beyond gaming into gamified consumer platforms, prediction markets and other onchain-native experiences, and a more capital-disciplined deployment posture given ARB price volatility.

Disclosed portfolio companies include Giant, Golden Tides, Forkast, The Lost Glitches, Coverd, Hyve Labs, Wildcard, T-Rex, Forge.gg, Jin Anomaly, XAI and Thousands.

Intake: AGV runs a standing expression of interest at arbitrumgamingventures.com/apply — 'If you are working on the next big thing in gaming, entertainment, or consumer, we want to hear from you. Apply to become a part of the AGV portfolio and bring your vision to life on Arbitrum.' There is no published deadline and no per-deal size is disclosed. The Arbitrum Foundation's grants index lists AGV as Active with a 'Submit Interest' button, 'Managed by The ArbitrumDAO'.

AGV was publicly launched under this name on 8 May 2025, in a press release revealing its first $10M investment cohort; arbitrumgamingventures.com was first captured five days later.

opportunities.description:
Rolling smart-contract bug bounty for Arcadia Finance, the margin-account lending protocol deployed on Base, Optimism and Unichain, hosted on HackenProof and triaged by the platform.

The HackenProof listing shows the program live since 10 June 2026 — its catalogue entry reports a last update on 30 June 2026 — with $1,250 paid across 105 submissions from 60 hackers. Every tier is an explicit ceiling with no floor — the program's own words: "the Max reward tier is the highest payout available for an asset, not a floor" — which is why this record's payouts are up-to rather than ranges: up to $25,000 for critical, up to $7,500 for high, up to $2,000 for medium; low findings are unrewarded and carry no tier here.

The program publishes unusually disciplined primacy-of-impact severity rules: recoverable or reversible losses never classify as critical, a single-user loss is capped at high, trusted roles and trusted third parties (Chainlink, CoW Protocol solvers) are out of scope, live on-chain state is the sole reference for realistic preconditions, and exposure-cap issues without realized loss grade as low or informational.

opportunities.title: Base Ecosystem Fund
opportunities.description:
"Base Ecosystem Fund is the strategic investment arm of Base. In partnership with Coinbase Ventures, we invest in pre-seed and seed stage startups that choose Base as their home. Our approach is borderless and uncompromisingly team-centric, focusing on accelerating the elite builders on Base." The fund positions itself as "Pairing early-stage capital with deep ecosystem alignment to ensure the best teams have the resources to achieve venture-scale growth from day one."

Mission: "to catalyze the Base economy by backing ambitious founders focused on delivering venture scale outcomes." Investment strategy: "We invest in the world's top talent building the next generation of enduring and high-performance onchain primitives & businesses that drive real economic activity and define the onchain future."

What portfolio companies get, in three published buckets: White Glove Support — "Hands-on support from our ecosystem team to unlock partner integrations and amplify distribution"; Exclusive Perks — "Unlock credits from our partners including AWS, Azure, Alchemy, Spindl ad credits and more"; and Coinbase Access — "Get priority access to Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Business, and Coinbase Onramp API".

The Ecosystem Fund is one rung of a published six-stage support ladder: (01) Idea — Base Batches, "Base's in-house Accelerator program"; (02) Pre-seed & Seed — Ecosystem Fund; (03) Growth — Coinbase Ventures; (04) Private Fundraise — Echo; (05) Public Token Sale — Sonar by Echo; (06) Listing — Coinbase. Teams at idea stage are therefore routed to Base Batches rather than to this fund.

Portfolio companies named on the page: Aerodrome, Avantis, Limitless, A0X, B3, BANKR, Berry, Blockrun, Boardwalk, Charms, Credit Coop, Crown, Ethos, Exactly Protocol, Flyra, Giza, Glider, HeyElsa, Jia, Kash, Kontigo, LiveFrame, Nuzo, Offramp, Onboard, OpenCover, Paragraph, Pred, Remix, Sapien, Senpi, Sport.Fun, Tailgate, Tenor, Truflation, Veil, ViFi, Wrapped CBDC and Zynk, filterable by Trading, Payments, AI Agents and Other.

Application is a multi-step form at base.org/ecosystem-fund/apply with sections for Company, Team, Idea, Funding and Why Base; the first step asks for Company Name, "What are you building?", Website URL and X URL. No fund size, check size, instrument, ownership target, deadline or decision timeline is published.

The fund was announced on 23 February 2023, in Coinbase's Base launch post: "We're also announcing the Base Ecosystem Fund, which invests in and supports early stage projects building on Base that meet our investment criteria. If you're interested, please fill out the form here." That is the entire announcement — it names no fund size, no check size and no target project count.

**Nothing about the money is published — and Base publishes it for its neighbouring programs.** The fund page carries no fund size, check size, instrument, ownership target or decision timeline; the launch announcement quoted above named none; and the first-cohort post quantifies only demand ("We received over 800 applications for our Base Ecosystem Fund") with no per-deal amounts for any of the six investments. Base's own funding documentation does publish ranges one rung either side — Builder Rewards "distributes 2 ETH weekly", Builder Grants a "Grant Range: 1-5 ETH" — but does not list the Ecosystem Fund at all: re-read on 2026-08-13, docs.base.org/get-started/get-funded covers Builder Rewards, Builder Grants, OP Retro Funding and Base Batches, and the Ecosystem Fund is absent from it. This record previously said the docs listed the fund without a figure, which is a different and weaker claim than the one the page supports. There is no earlier version to fall back on either: the fund page has never been archived. The absence is the fund's own posture, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.

opportunities.title: Cap Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for Cap, the stablecoin protocol behind cUSD that secures collateral for borrowing operations through the Symbiotic and EigenLayer shared-security networks, hosted on Sherlock and scoped to Ethereum mainnet only.

The Sherlock listing shows the program live since 24 October 2025, with a $1,000,000 maximum for a critical finding, capped at 10% of funds at risk at the time of submission. Only vulnerabilities in the core contracts — AccessControl, Delegation, FeeAuction, FeeReceiver, Oracle, Lender, Vault, FractionalReserve and Minter, plus their inherited contracts — qualify for the critical severity. The program accepts High submissions (they carry the same 250 deposit as criticals) but publishes no figure for them: rewards are decided on validation by Sherlock "up to the caps listed above", which is why the high tier in this record's table is discretionary rather than numbered. Low and informational findings are not eligible.

Severity and validity are judged by Sherlock. Front-end issues are judged at the Cap team's discretion, and Gelato, external protocol integrations and known audit issues are out of scope.

fundingDetails.severityScheme: The programme's own severity definitions published in the Sherlock brief (Critical: definite significant loss or >1-year freeze of funds, core contracts only), judged by Sherlock

opportunities.title: Ethereum Foundation Bug Bounty Program
opportunities.description:
The Ethereum Foundation's rolling bug bounty for consensus and execution-layer specs, the major client implementations (Geth, Reth, Nethermind, Erigon, Besu, Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Lodestar, Grandine), Solidity and Vyper, and the deposit contract.

The ethereum.org bug bounty page confirms the program is 'Open for submissions' with no end date and severity tiers reaching $1,000,000 for a critical finding, submitted through the Foundation's own report form.

The program was introduced publicly on 18 December 2014, in the Foundation's blog post "A call to all the bug bounty hunters out there…", which opened bounties on the protocols, the Go implementation and the network code; a follow-up in March 2015 confirms it running from around that time.

fundingDetails.severityScheme: Ethereum Foundation bug bounty vulnerability severity qualifications (validator-slashing / network-split / network-liveness thresholds)

opportunities.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's rolling protocol and client bug bounty, paying up to $1,000,000 for a critical finding.
opportunities.eligibility: Awards cannot be issued to individuals on sanctions lists or resident in countries on sanctions lists. Proof of identity is required by local law, and the reporter is responsible for all taxes. Employees, contractors, service providers or grantees of the Ethereum Foundation, and members of client teams in scope, may accrue leaderboard points only and receive no monetary reward during the relationship and for 90 days after it ends. Determinations of eligibility and award are at the sole discretion of the Ethereum Foundation bug bounty panel.
opportunities.prerequisites: A reproducible proof of concept is mandatory: either a Kurtosis-based PoC that spins up a local devnet, or a state test (EVM/goevmlab); plain unit tests are not accepted. For Solidity/Vyper compiler bugs a Kurtosis or state test is not required, but the triggering source, the exact affected compiler versions, a comparison against a working version and step-by-step reproduction are. A burn in ETH is required to submit a report as an anti-spam measure, and there are no refunds. Reports without a PoC, already submitted by another reporter, already known to spec or client maintainers, or publicly disclosed beforehand, are ineligible.
opportunities.additionalReferences: In scope: protocol soundness (consensus model, wire and p2p protocols, proof of stake), the Consensus Layer and Execution Layer specifications, execution-layer clients (Besu, Erigon, Geth, Nethermind, Reth) and consensus-layer clients (Lighthouse, Lodestar, Nimbus, Teku, Prysm, Grandine), the Solidity and Vyper compilers, the Beacon Chain deposit contract specification and source, and the dependencies C-KZG-4844 and Go-KZG-4844. Out of scope: infrastructure such as webpages, DNS and email; ERC-20 contract bugs; ENS bugs; issues requiring a publicly exposed API such as JSON-RPC or the Beacon API; the Engine API, which is treated as trusted; typographical errors; tests; high-effort single-peer DoS; publicly known issues; and anything without direct impact on Ethereum mainnet. Programme rules and scope: https://ethereum.org/bug-bounty/ (bounty.ethereum.org redirects here). Submission form: https://bbp-form.ethereum.org/ . A public leaderboard of past reporters is published on the rules page. Program announcement (18 December 2014): https://blog.ethereum.org/2014/12/18/call-bug-bounty-hunters.

opportunities.title: Ecosystem Support Program (ESP)
opportunities.description:
The Ecosystem Support Program (ESP) is an ecosystem-development cluster inside the Ethereum Foundation made up of two teams: Grant Management (allocating resources to the projects most critical to Ethereum's resilience and usability) and Funding Coordination (making it simpler and faster for impactful projects to secure funding, including co-funding work with Octant, Gitcoin and ENS DAO).

ESP supports free, open-source, non-commercial work directed at builders rather than end users: Ethereum infrastructure, builder tooling, cryptographic research, education and community development.

**Application process (six steps, rolling, no deadline):**
1. **Browse** the Wishlist or the RFP list and find an item matching your expertise. Wishlist items name gaps and invite you to propose an approach; RFP items are more prescriptive and time-bound around a defined deliverable.
2. **Apply** with a proposal covering methodology, timeline and deliverables. You receive a confirmation email.
3. **Review** by the Grant Management (GM) team together with the EF team that owns the item. May include an interview, project rescoping or budget negotiation.
4. **Decision** by email. Most applications are reviewed within **3-6 weeks**. Selected projects agree a grant structure with **milestone-based payments**, then complete onboarding including identity verification and a formal grant letter.
5. **Execute** with a Grant Evaluator assigned for regular check-ins and milestone reviews.
6. **Complete** by publishing the results publicly in a report or post.

**Funding size:** ESP publishes no fixed award range. Per the ESP FAQ, "Grant funding is determined based on the scope and complexity of the proposal, unless otherwise specified in the posted Wishlist or RFP item. Where applicable, RFPs may include budget guidance estimates. The GM team will work with applicants to determine final grant amounts."

**Payment:** "Ethereum Foundation grants are paid on-chain in ETH by default", and recipients must be able to securely receive and manage ETH. Exceptions are considered only in limited cases where legal or operational constraints prevent receiving ETH.

ESP's own published allocation history: 136 projects / $26.9M (2021), 397 projects / $30.0M (2022), 498 projects / $61.1M (2023), 677 projects / $44.4M (2024).

You may apply to multiple Wishlist or RFP items, but each needs a separate application.

ESP was introduced on the Ethereum Foundation blog on 19 November 2019 — "Introducing the Ecosystem Support Program", published together with a call for applications directing applicants to esp.ethereum.foundation. That is the earliest ESP post on the blog and the date this record carries as `postedAt`.

**On the figures this record does not carry.** The allocation history above is historic disbursement, not a budget: ESP publishes no annual envelope, no round envelope — "There are no active grant rounds at this time" — and no per-grant range, and the FAQ quoted above declines to give one. The only ceiling ESP ever published belonged to the Small Grants track, "Small grants, capped at $30,000", and that track no longer exists: the page returns 404 and it is absent from the current sitemap, so it is not a current ceiling for anything. Budget guidance, where it exists at all, lives inside individual Wishlist or RFP items rather than at program level, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.

operatingOrganizations.name: Ethereum Foundation
operatingOrganizations.description: Stiftung Ethereum, a Swiss Stiftung (foundation) located at Zeughausgasse 7a, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. It operates ethereum.org, ethereum.foundation, esp.ethereum.foundation, devcon.org, devconnect.org and blog.ethereum.org. The Ecosystem Support Program is an ecosystem-development cluster within the Foundation, comprising the Grant Management and Funding Coordination teams.

opportunities.summary: Rolling Ethereum Foundation grants for open-source public goods, applied for against a public Wishlist or a defined RFP.
opportunities.eligibility: Applications are evaluated on: **Technical approach** (soundness, feasibility and clarity of the proposed methodology and implementation plan); **Ecosystem impact** (potential benefit to the Ethereum community and alignment with ecosystem priorities); **Open source** — "All outputs must be open-source or otherwise freely available; for-profit companies are welcome to apply, but the specific grant-funded work must be open-source and accessible to the community"; **Budget** (cost-effectiveness, and "since we are offering non-dilutive capital, we generally anticipate some flexibility below standard market rates"); **Experience** (relevant background, skills and prior work); and **Alignment** (understanding of Ethereum's values and ecosystem needs). ESP support is generally directed toward enabling builders rather than end-users.
opportunities.prerequisites: A proposal must be tied to a specific published Wishlist or RFP item and must detail how you plan to address it, including your methodology, timeline and deliverables, plus how your background and approach align with the project requirements. Separate applications are required for each item. Grant recipients must complete identity verification, sign a formal grant letter, and be able to securely receive and manage on-chain ETH payments.
opportunities.additionalReferences: Program site: https://esp.ethereum.foundation/ — introduction and first call for applications (19 November 2019): https://blog.ethereum.org/2019/11/19/ecosystem-support-program-call-for-applications

opportunities.title: Lido Ecosystem Grants Organisation (LEGO)
opportunities.description:
LEGO (Lido Ecosystem Grants Organization) funds individuals, projects and initiatives that benefit the Lido protocol and the broader blockchain space — developers, crypto enthusiasts and community members with a plan to improve the ecosystem or raise awareness about Ethereum, proof-of-stake and DeFi.

**Grant classification — four tiers, all quoted in USD.** LEGO grants are "sorted into four different piles by expected size and impact". The tier determines who approves the grant, not when it may be submitted:

| Tier | Description | Approver | Grant amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sandgrain** | Contributions that are nice to have, yet not detrimental. Can be easily evaluated by a single person. | 1 member | up to 1,000 USD |
| **Pebble** | Non-critical, small things that are beneficial for Lido but not so trivial as to call a sand grain. | 2 members | up to 10,000 USD |
| **Boulder** | Big, important things that are imperative to be carried out by experts and thoroughly evaluated by core contributors. | Council vote | up to 100,000 USD |
| **Mountain** | Critical improvements to Lido with significant impact on its growth, security, operations, etc. | DAO vote | 100,000 USD + |

The Mountain tier has no published upper bound, so the 100,000 USD figure recorded as the maximum award is the top of the Boulder tier — the largest tier with a stated cap.

**Application process (rolling, no deadlines):**
1. **Contact** — reach the LEGO person responsible for your area of contribution (or any LEGO person, who will forward you) on **Telegram** to introduce yourself and your idea.
2. **Discuss grant terms** — hash out terms, timelines and deliverables in personal communication with the relevant LEGO member, who takes it through the LEGO approval process.
3. **Review** — the proposal is shared on the Lido research forum (research.lido.fi) and among LEGO committee members. On approval, communication channels are set up and the nominee receives funding.
4. **Present** — on completion, the creator presents the work to the LEGO committee.

Execution timelines vary by grant size and by how many committee members must take part.

**Committee:** LEGO has two segments. The **LEGO Council** is 8 partners, each responsible for a segment of Lido, each with a capacity of 15,000 LDO equivalent per quarter to fund sandgrain- and pebble-sized grants; only the Council votes on Boulders. **LEGO Nominees** are up to 20 individuals with a personal budget of 10,000 LDO equivalent per quarter (included in the total LEGO budget), managed by a vote of the LEGO Council. Any LEGO member can send a sandgrain, coordinate on pebbles and motion towards Boulders.

LEGO issues detailed quarterly reports on all granting activity at lego.lido.fi.

LEGO was introduced on the Lido research forum on 10 March 2021, in the topic "Project: Lido Ecosystem Grants Organization" — "a draft of the program for funding Lido ecosystem development with grants from the Lido Treasury".

opportunities.title: Mantle EcoFund
opportunities.description:
The Mantle EcoFund is Mantle's ecosystem investment vehicle for early-stage projects seeking a long-term partnership with Mantle Network. It was established by Mantle governance proposal MIP-24, posted to the Mantle forum on 26 February 2023, which 'authorized the establishment of a US$100 million Mantle EcoFund capitalised by the Mantle Treasury'; capital is drawn down in tranches through governance-approved capital calls denominated in USDC (a first call of US$10 million, then a second call of US$30 million authorised by MIP-29 in February 2024, which also expanded the fund's investment mandate). Mantle's own site currently describes the EcoFund as having 'a $200M catalyzed capital pool… accessing top-tier deal flow through 20 leading VCs like Polychain and Dragonfly' — that larger figure is the catalysed pool including co-investor capital, not the DAO-authorised fund size. Mirana Ventures plays a strategic role supporting the fund.

This is investment and partnership support rather than a fixed grant cheque. Investment criteria, in Mantle's words, look for projects that are early stage; are seeking a long-term partnership with Mantle; can attract capital from venture firms and allocators; and synergize with other Mantle Ecosystem partners.

Support provided is split into two tiers. Exclusively for EcoFund portfolio companies: the EcoFund 'EF' tag, and deal-structuring and fundraising support. Prioritized for them (and also provided to top-performing applications on Mantle generally): Mantle co-promotion on media, social and events; enhanced delegated voting; listing recommendations to partnered exchanges; liquidity support via the Economics Committee program; and direct access and regular catch-ups with the Mantle Growth team.

Intake is by email rather than a public form: the EcoFund page's 'Contact Us' resolves to ecofund@mantle.xyz, with the suggested subject line 'Join Mantle EcoFund as a Strategic Venture Partner'. The page lists 40+ portfolio companies across DeFi, gaming, Bitcoin infrastructure, RWA and AI, many tagged 'Live'. No closing date is published. Historic selectivity disclosed in governance: between 1 September 2023 and 15 January 2024 the EcoFund team reviewed 252 projects, took 58 (23%) into deeper due diligence, and invested in 10 (3.9%).

opportunities.title: MetaMask Grants Program
opportunities.description:
MetaMask Grants DAO is an employee-led, Consensys-funded DAO whose mission is to fund the development of high-value projects in the MetaMask ecosystem, supporting developers across the community to build on top of MetaMask while empowering Consensys employees to embrace web3 mechanisms.

**Structure — three parts:**
1. **Employee-Led DAO** — the body of the DAO, made up of full-time Consensys employees, with a stated intent to decentralize over time and add external contributors.
2. **Leadership Committee (mini-DAO)** — 7 individuals responsible for finding high-potential projects, creating governance proposals, updating external content, gathering feedback and queuing multisig transactions. If a member leaves Consensys, the remaining members may fill the seat by majority vote. Members are Dan Finlay, Aaron Davis (Kumavis), Taylor Monahan, Christian Montoya, Ryan Jones, Ian Wallis and Jordan Spence.
3. **Secure MultiSig** — a 2-of-3 Gnosis Safe controlled by Consensys that manages the token contract and treasury and signs disbursements.

**Two grant types:**
- **Leadership Committee Grants** — voted on exclusively by the Leadership Committee. Any Committee member may propose; proposals with at least **5 'yes' votes** at closing pass. Votes are open for **five days**.
- **Full DAO Grants** — voted on by the full DAO. Any Committee member may propose; proposals with more 'yes' than 'no' votes at closing pass. Votes are open for **ten days**.

Voting occurs on Activate, Consensys' proprietary platform built on top of Snapshot (the DAO's Snapshot space is `heart.mmgdao.eth`). Governance uses a non-transferable, fungible mainnet token that is mintable and burnable by the multisig and is "explicitly designed to never be exchanged for value"; all Consensys employees receive the same number of tokens, minted on joining and burned on departure.

**Intake:** external developers apply via a rolling application form. The DAO's Request for Proposals page states: "We are not currently running any RFP rounds, but our rolling grant applications remain open." There is no guaranteed review timeline — "We can't guarantee when we will review your request or that it will get approved, but know that our team will review the application pipeline as often as we can."

**No published range, and no envelope.** Nothing on the DAO's own site carries a dollar figure — not the FAQ's description of the two grant types, not the RFP page, not the grantee list. The closest it comes is a DAO objective stating that "More than 50% of the DAO's initial budget is allocated through tokenized proposal voting within the first three months of operation": the phrase "initial budget", without the number. Its Snapshot space holds sixteen proposals in total, of which three state an amount, and each states it as that grant's own size ($36,000, $35,000, $35,000) rather than as a range the program publishes. Consensys' launch announcement put the DAO's first-year funding at $2.4M, but that is the funder's press release rather than the program's own published budget, so this record carries no `fundingInfo` rather than promote it into one. The treasury cannot be read instead: it is described only as a 2-of-3 Gnosis Safe controlled by Consensys, with no address published anywhere on the site.

**On the open status:** the DAO's own RFP page still states that rolling grant applications remain open, which is what this record follows. Its Snapshot space has had no proposal since 22 December 2023, so the intake is open and the governance around it is quiet.

The DAO was launched on 27 October 2022, announced by Consensys as issuing grants to developers worldwide; metamaskgrants.org was first captured the same day.

opportunities.title: MetaMask Validator Staking Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for the smart contracts behind MetaMask Portfolio's 32-ETH Validator Staking — the Kiln On-Chain v1 staking contracts — hosted on HackenProof and triaged by the platform.

The HackenProof listing shows the program live since 18 March 2024 — its catalogue entry reports a last update on 15 May 2026 — with rewards denominated in ETH: 20-200 ETH for a critical finding (the platform's sidebar renders that as roughly $70,000-$700,000 at current prices), 5-20 ETH for high, 1-5 ETH for medium and 0.25-1 ETH for low. The critical rule is published: 10% of the funds directly affected, calculated at report-submission time, capped at the table maximum with the table minimum as a guaranteed floor; high rewards are capped at 100% of the funds affected within their range.

The scope is deliberately narrow: the mainnet staking contract at 0xdc71affc862fceb6ad32be58e098423a7727bebd (no proxy) and the pinned kilnfi/staking-contracts repository at commit f33eb8d. The portfolio.metamask.io web application is explicitly out of scope, as are known issues from the program's three published audits. The listing reports 262 submissions from 131 hackers and **$0 in total rewards paid** — a live program that has yet to validate a paying finding.

opportunities.title: Midas Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for Midas, a platform for composable onchain investment products that turns institutional strategies into compliant tokens composable across DeFi protocols such as Morpho and Pendle, hosted on Sherlock.

The Sherlock listing shows the program live since 19 May 2026, with a headline maximum of $500,000 — the Ethereum-contract Critical ceiling. The reward table splits four ways: **Ethereum contracts** (Critical $25,000-$500,000, High $5,000-$25,000, Medium flat $5,000, Low $500-$1,000), **Solana contracts**, **contract configuration** and the **web interface** (the latter two each: Critical $2,500-$50,000, High $500-$2,500, Medium $250-$500). The Solana sub-scope (critical $10,000-$200,000 down to low $250-$500, hard-capped at $400,000) is real but sits outside this dataset's Ethereum-ecosystem scope, so this record's structured tier table carries the Ethereum-side scopes only and the Solana figures live in this prose.

The arithmetic behind the contract Critical tiers is published: "the reward amount will be calculated as 10% of the funds directly affected, up to the maximum cap defined in the applicable reward range", assessed at submission time, with a minimum reward granted to discourage withholding — and a vulnerability must place at least $10,000 at direct risk to classify as Critical at all. High-severity rewards are capped at up to 100% of the funds directly affected within their ranges. The program also publishes hard caps per scope — $1M Ethereum contracts, $400,000 Solana contracts, $100,000 configuration, $100,000 web — with total payouts never exceeding $1,000,000, allocated first-come-first-served by submission timestamp if cumulative valid reports would exceed a cap.

Chains in scope are Ethereum mainnet, Base, Optimism and Moonbeam; the program publishes an unusually thorough known-issues list, from Wormhole-dependency failure modes for its multichain governance to specific reward-accrual quirks, all ineligible.

opportunities.title: Nouns DAO Small Grants
opportunities.description:
The Nouns DAO Small Grants Committee was created by **Nouns proposal 13**. It is run by a group of Nouners to be a "flexible pool of capital" that can be deployed when the project is time-sensitive, when the ask is too small for an official Nouns DAO proposal, or when retroactive funding is merited because the work is already done.

The committee's own scope statement is **"For projects needing 0.1-10Ξ"** — grants are denominated natively in ETH. The published grants ledger shows individual awards from 0.025Ξ up to 27.25Ξ, with USD equivalents shown alongside for reference only. (Re-read 2026-08-13: the ledger's low end is 0.025Ξ, below the committee's own stated 0.1Ξ floor, with several awards at 0.05Ξ. This record previously gave the low end as 0.1 ETH, which is the scope statement rather than what the ledger shows.)

**Two funding modes:**
- **Small Grant** — an upfront payment to fund a project.
- **Retroactive Funding** — a payment for work already completed.

**Requesting a grant:** open a post on the Nouns Discourse forum and prefix the title with "Small Grants: " for visibility. A committee member will then reach out to you, but you can also post the link to your Discourse post in the **#grants-and-retro-funding** channel in the Nouns Discord to get it on their radar. There are no deadlines.

**⚠️ Verification note (re-checked 2026-08-13):** the Discourse forum that this process depends on no longer exists — `discourse.nouns.wtf` returns no DNS record at all, and neither does `forum.nouns.wtf` — so every historical "Small Grants:" thread linked from the instructions is unreachable. The instructions page at nouns.center is live (HTTP 200) and unchanged, still headed "For projects needing 0.1-10Ξ" and still routing applicants to Discourse; `nouns.wtf` resolves and the Nouns Discord invite still resolves. So the documented primary submission venue is dead while the page documenting it is not.

**Why this record is `closed`, and what that status does and does not claim.** No page states that the committee has wound down, and none states that it is still awarding. The status here is a reading of the last verifiable evidence rather than a funder announcement: the only intake route the committee publishes cannot be reached, and nothing published replaces it. It is not a claim that the committee has been dissolved. For the same reason this record carries no `deadlines`: the committee's own instructions say there are no deadlines, which was previously recorded as a rolling application deadline, but a rolling intake is a claim about an open programme and this record is not asserting one. Prospective applicants should confirm the current route in the Nouns Discord, which is the one contact point on the instructions page that still resolves, before relying on these instructions.

Proposal 13, "Retroactive Funding and Small Grants Pool", was proposed on 19 October 2021 by noun22.eth, which is the date this record carries as `postedAt`.

opportunities.title: Polymarket Builders Program
opportunities.description:
The Polymarket Builders Program offers **over $2.5M in grants** for developers building apps, tools and experiments on top of Polymarket. Amounts are quoted only in US dollars on the program page; the associated weekly builder rewards are explicitly paid in USDC, which Polymarket settles in.

Grants: 'Grants are distributed to the best teams based on product innovation and traction.' Polymarket names the kinds of projects it wants — integrating Polymarket markets inside your app; distributing to a specific vertical or geography; building a pro trading terminal with advanced orders; empowering users with new analytics, portfolio managers and AI decisions; launching a new type of media powered by prediction markets; or creating DeFi primitives such as lending and vaults. A 'Request for Builders' page (builders.polymarket.com/rfb) publishes the team's own idea list — explicitly framed as a prompt rather than a constraint. Support includes technical support and amplification on Polymarket's social channels.

Weekly rewards: separately from grants, 'the most active builders earn extra weekly rewards based on volume'. Polymarket describes it as a weekly USDC rewards program launched to bootstrap Builder Codes integrations, paid on integration volume. Each reward epoch runs from Sunday 00:00 UTC to Saturday 23:59 UTC. Builder Codes are unique credentials that let builders attribute orders to their builder profile and grant access to the Polymarket Relayer API; volume is credited for every matched trade attributed to the builder account and appears on the public Builder Leaderboard within about 24 hours. No per-epoch pool size or payout formula is published. As of 2026-08-11 the leaderboard's top integration shows ~$40.04M of 1-month volume.

Joining is permissionless — 'Polymarket DeFi protocol is free and permissionless to use and access. Just start building to be part of the program!' — and there is no deadline. The grant application is an in-page form on builders.polymarket.com.

Polymarket published no announcement post for the program, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the Builders Program site was publicly visible by 2 November 2025, its first capture, which is also the start of the weekly builder-rewards program it runs alongside.

opportunities.title: RFP: Reboot the Gitcoin Community for the 3.3 Era
opportunities.description:
A vendor solicitation posted to the Gitcoin DAO governance forum on 13 May 2026 by owocki. Header block as published: "Issued by: Gitcoin DAO (sponsor: Kevin Owocki, ED) · Date issued: May 2026 · Proposals due: Rolling, first review June 1, 2026 · Engagement window: June 2026 – Q1 2027 (phased; see milestones) · Budget envelope: Open — propose your number. Bias toward lean, milestone-gated engagements over a single large retainer. · Submit to: kevin@gitcoin.co and/or post a response on gov.gitcoin.co".

Context given: "Gitcoin is entering its 3.3 era… The DAO controls ~$20M in treasury + matching pool; ~12M GTC is held by the DAO and needs to be re-delegated back to a real, engaged community of delegates. We are looking for one or more vendors / collectives / individuals to run a phased community reboot. You may bid on one, two, or all three. We expect to award multiple contracts."

WORKSTREAM A — DELEGATION: recruit 10–30 GTC delegates capable of carrying ~2.5M GTC of voting power (target ~100K–250K GTC per delegate, with a long tail). Proposal threshold is 150K GTC; quorum is 2.5M GTC (GovernorBravo 0x9d4c63565d5618310271bf3f3c01b2954c1d1639). Scope: build a candidate pipeline sourced from the existing Gitcoin community, allied DAOs (Optimism, Arbitrum, ENS, Protocol Guild, Octant), Ethereum public-goods orgs, AI-livelihood-aligned operators, regen/impact orgs and returning Gitcoin alumni; vet candidates against a public rubric covering mission alignment, governance track record, time commitment, conflicts, and geographic and ideological diversity; produce delegate profiles on Tally and gov.gitcoin.co; run delegate onboarding (GTC mechanics, treasury landscape, the 3.3 mission, open proposals, cadence expectations); and coordinate the delegation events themselves, matching candidates with GTC holders and getting the transactions executed. Deliverables: public rubric and selection process; 10–30 onboarded, publicly-profiled delegates with active GTC delegated; a live delegate roster with bios, conflicts and contact; a delegate orientation handbook (one-pager plus 30-min recorded onboarding); and a quarterly delegate health check. Success metrics: ≥ 2.5M GTC actively delegated to non-Foundation, non-multisig addresses within 90 days of contract start; no single delegate holding > 20% of active delegated supply; ≥ 70% of active delegates voting on at least 80% of proposals in their first 6 months. Gitcoin provides introductions (Foundation, Kyle Weiss, Owocki, existing top delegates), social amplification, coordination with Mathilda on contract/Governor parameters, and a pool of GTC the Foundation and Kevin are willing to delegate (subject to separate approval).

WORKSTREAM B — EDUCATION: re-onboard the community to Gitcoin 3.3 and open a first door for net-new audiences (AI-economy operators, livelihood-focused funders, post-Web3 builders). Scope: a 6–8 week educational series across at least three formats — weekly or biweekly Twitter/X Spaces of ~45–60 min (Kevin plus co-host explainers, debates with critics, deep-dives with builders), monthly async-friendly AMAs on gov.gitcoin.co or elsewhere with a written summary published within 48h, and one additional format of the bidder's choice (podcast, YouTube longform, in-person at events, IRL salons, workshops, university chapters); a canonical "Gitcoin 3.3 in 10 minutes" explainer in video and written form; an FAQ on gov.gitcoin.co absorbing questions surfaced in Spaces/AMAs; and 3–5 seeded third-party explainers. Deliverables: a published calendar of educational events; ≥ 20 Twitter Spaces and ≥ 6 AMAs over the 6-month engagement; the canonical explainer; a maintained FAQ with ≥ 50 entries; and 3–5 third-party content placements. Success metrics: cumulative attended-live audience across Spaces ≥ 15K and cumulative replays ≥ 100K; ≥ 100 new gov.gitcoin.co accounts and ≥ 100 new GTC delegations attributable to educational programming; ≥ 25 pieces of independent third-party content referencing Gitcoin 3.3; ≥ 10 inbound asks per month citing educational content as the entry point. Gitcoin provides Kevin's time (cap ~3 hrs/week public-facing), talent introductions, brand assets, and its forum and social channels.

WORKSTREAM C — CAMPAIGN: a launch campaign plan for Gitcoin 3.3, targeted at ~Q4 2026 / Q1 2027. Explicitly: "We are not procuring execution of the campaign today. We are procuring the campaign plan, with an option to execute pending mutual agreement closer to launch." The plan must cover an audience map (delegates, builders, funders, beneficiaries, press, allied DAOs, each with its call-to-action); narrative architecture over a ~6-week launch window with hero artifacts; a channel plan (X, Farcaster, podcasts, conference presence including Devcon, partner co-marketing, paid if justified, press); mechanism activation driving at least one measurable on-chain event; a risk plan covering low turnout, hostile takes, technical delay and AI-livelihood backlash; budget and team, with pricing for the plan separate from pricing for execution; and proposed KPIs. Deliverables: a written plan of 2–5 pages delivered no later than 90 days before target launch, one review session with Kevin, Mathilda, Julia, Ash and ≥ 2 advisors, and an optional bid to execute.

WHO THEY WANT: community-organizing operators with DAO governance experience; editorial/media collectives with crypto-native distribution and a record of moving narrative "(not just impressions)"; individual operators with deep Ethereum public-goods relationships; and cross-movement organizers from outside crypto (AI safety, livelihood/labor, post-growth, regen). Explicitly not fits: "pure paid-media agencies, 'growth hacking' shops, generic web3 marketing firms, anyone whose primary offer is follower count."

REVIEW PROCESS: "Rolling. First batch reviewed June 1, 2026 by Kevin + Mathilda + ≥ 1 advisor. Shortlisted vendors get a call. Decisions announced on gov.gitcoin.co."

The posting carries four open questions bidders are asked to address, and a standing caveat: "This RFP is a living document. It will be updated as the working groups (education: Julia; funding/recruitment: Mathilda; marketing: Ash) refine scope," plus a disclaimer that it "is for informative purposes only… reflects my personal views, not a decision or commitment by Gitcoin governance."

As of 2026-08-11 the forum thread is still titled "DRAFT - RFP: Reboot the Gitcoin Community for the 3.3 Era", carries no tags, and is neither closed nor archived. It has five posts; the last was 2026-06-05. Four public bid summaries have been posted (SEEDGov, Anode/Kaf, Tanisha Katara of Katara Consulting Group, and Eureka/Sixty), all bidding on Workstream A with partial bids on B and C. No award, shortlist or decision has been announced on the thread.

**The open budget is the RFP's design, not a missing field.** Beyond the header's "Budget envelope: Open — propose your number", the RFP pushes pricing onto bidders everywhere it could have set a ceiling: "Budget and milestone structure. Prefer milestone-gated payments"; "Budget and team. What you'd need to execute. Pricing for the plan should be separate from pricing for execution"; and, among its open questions, "What's your honest read on the MVP budget that produces real signal vs. theater?" No range, per-workstream cap or per-milestone amount appears anywhere. The only dollar figure in the document is context about the DAO's own finances (~$20M in treasury plus matching pool), not this engagement's envelope. Of the four bids posted to the thread, three state that the priced proposal went to the sponsor by email and one published its own ask — $5,000 total, split across two milestones — which is a bidder's price and not the program's, so nothing is recorded from it.

opportunities.title: Road to Devcon 8 India — Ecosystem Program
opportunities.description:
A Request for Proposals run by the Ethereum Foundation's Ecosystem Support Program (ESP) in the run-up to Devcon 8 (3–6 November 2026, Jio World Centre, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai, India).

The program "supports grassroots initiatives that contribute to the Ethereum ecosystem's growth and resilience ahead of Devcon 8… empowering local projects, builders, and ecosystem contributors to create meaningful spaces for learning, experimentation, and coordination, both online and in-person." Supported formats are "meetups, bootcamps, hackathons, roundtables, academic collaborations, and other formats" that bring new people into Ethereum, strengthen connections across open source communities and the broader technology ecosystem, and encourage hands-on participation and knowledge sharing around CROPS.

Stated need: expanding access to Ethereum for new and diverse audiences and lowering barriers to entry through education, experimentation and local initiatives; bridging Ethereum with open source communities; and "Promoting and putting into practice Ethereum's core values, including: Censorship Resistance, Open Source, Privacy, and Security, through hands-on experiences" — the CROPS acronym the RFP tests applicants against.

Support on offer: "Up to $300 USD in financial support"; "Visibility and amplification across Devcon channels"; "Non-financial support (connections, guidance, coordination)"; and "Limited Devcon tickets (free or discounted), based on contribution and availability", capped at 5 per request. "Approved grants under this initiative are paid on-chain in ETH by default." Estimated project duration is listed as N/A. ESP tags the RFP "Community Growth" and "Ecosystem".

Application window: Opens Jul 3, 2026 · Closes Aug 14, 2026. Applicants apply through the ESP RFP apply route and are asked to follow the published Google Docs submission form.

**The window on this record is a re-run.** The same RFP page first opened on 25 March 2026 and closed on 20 April 2026 — that first opening is what `postedAt` records, which is why it precedes the July–August window above.

opportunities.title: Rocket Pool GMC Grants — Round 40
opportunities.description:
Round 40 of the Rocket Pool Grants Management Committee (GMC) grants track. Grants are for applicants who wish to **carry out the work themselves** — as distinct from bounties, which are open-ended goals that could be met by anyone, including parties other than the proposer.

**Round 40 schedule (from the call for applications):**
- Application Period: **August 7 - September 7, 2026**
- Scoring Deadline: **September 22, 2026**
- Final Voting Amendments, Discussion and Finalization: **September 23 - September 26, 2026**
- Award Announcement: **September 27, 2026**

**Submission mechanics:** applications are posted as **replies in the round's own forum thread** on the Rocket Pool DAO Discourse, using the published grant application template. "Only those grant applications that are posted in this thread and timestamped by September 7, 2026 at 23:59 (11:59 PM) UTC will be considered. Any grants posted after that deadline will be carried over to the next award period." Questions and discussion of submitted applications go in a separate community discussion thread, not the application thread.

**GMC goals.** Grants, bounties and retrospective awards should make it easier and/or more attractive to do one or more of the following: become a node operator; operate a node, mint rETH; hold or use rETH; improve the quality of life for the protocol and its community.

**Grants scoring rubric.** When evaluating grant applications the GMC considers: (1) if the application is successful, to what extent does it further the GMC goals; (2) to what extent can the application be feasibly carried out by the person(s) proposed to complete it; (3) if the application is successful, how large is the benefit to the protocol relative to the size of the proposed costs.

**Award sizing.** The GMC publishes no per-grant cap. Applicants state their own ask, and the application template asks it **in US dollars**: "How much USD $ and over what period of time is the applicant requesting?" Payment is made from the committee's RPL treasury — the July 2026 treasury report notes that month's payments were made at an RPL price of $1.77, and the committee separately executes RPL-to-USDC swaps to settle awards. The GMC can only send grants directly to a recipient address and cannot accept invoices.

**Microgrants.** Following a GMC vote, a microgrant framework was introduced (announced May 2026) in response to treasury constraints. Microgrants use the existing GMC grant system with no process changes and no separate application type — contributors submit standard applications and the GMC may choose to award a microgrant. Microgrants "will typically fall into one of the following ranges: 10 RPL, 50 RPL, 100 RPL". They can be used for both new submissions and retrospective recognition, are intended as partial recognition given current constraints, may be revisited if treasury conditions improve, and there is no limit on how many a contributor can receive.

Because the applicant's ask is denominated in USD while microgrant tiers are quoted natively in RPL, and neither constitutes a published program-wide award range, no minAward/maxAward or currency is asserted on this record.

Round 40 is confirmed as the current round as of 2026-08-11: it is the most recent call for applications in the Grants / Bounties category, posted 2026-08-08, and no later round has superseded it.

The governing RPIP sets no per-grant cap and no per-round pool either; its only budget statement points upstream, to the share of the protocol-level budget set aside for grants and bounties together. Nothing at this record's level has ever been published as a number, which is why it carries no `fundingInfo`.
