opportunities.title: Rocket Pool GMC Retrospective Awards — Round 40
opportunities.description:
Round 40 of the Rocket Pool Grants Management Committee (GMC) **retrospective awards** track — recognition for work that has already been completed, as opposed to the grants track, which funds work an applicant proposes to carry out. The round covers Rocket Pool's **July 7, 2026 - September 7, 2026 retrospective awards**.

**Round 40 schedule (identical to the grants track):**
- Application Period: **August 7 - September 7, 2026**
- Scoring Deadline: **September 22, 2026**
- Final Voting Amendments, Discussion and Finalization: **September 23 - September 26, 2026**
- Award Announcement: **September 27, 2026**

**Submission mechanics:** applications are posted as **replies in the round's own retrospective-applications forum thread** on the Rocket Pool DAO Discourse, using the published retrospective award template. "Only those retrospective award applications that are posted in this thread and timestamped by September 7, 2026 at 23:59 (11:59 PM) UTC will be considered. Any retrospective award applications posted after that deadline will be carried over to the next award period." Questions and discussion of submitted applications go in a separate community discussion thread.

**GMC goals.** Grants, bounties and retrospective awards should make it easier and/or more attractive to do one or more of the following: become a node operator; operate a node, mint rETH; hold or use rETH; improve the quality of life for the protocol and its community.

**Retrospective award rubric — a single criterion:** "To what extent did the proposed and completed project further the GMC goals?" With the note: if the project is ongoing, the retrospective award is given for work completed prior to the current award period, and any future awards for the same project are expected to compete in the Grants category as a separate application. This is a narrower rubric than the three-part grants rubric, which also weighs feasibility and cost-benefit — feasibility is moot for work already delivered.

**Award sizing.** No per-award cap is published. The template asks the applicant to state the ask **in US dollars**: "How much USD $ is the applicant requesting be awarded to the recipient?" Awards are settled from the committee's RPL treasury, which receives 16,265.35 RPL every 28 days under RPIP-81, shared across the grants, bounty and retrospective tracks. The microgrant framework introduced in May 2026 applies to this track too — microgrants "can be used for both new submissions and retrospective recognition" and typically fall into 10 RPL, 50 RPL or 100 RPL tiers. Because the ask is denominated in USD while microgrant tiers are quoted natively in RPL, and neither is a published program-wide award range, no minAward/maxAward or currency is asserted on this record.

Round 40 is confirmed as the current round as of 2026-08-11: it is the most recent call for retrospective applications in the Grants / Bounties category, posted 2026-08-08.

**No ceiling governs this track (re-verified 2026-08-13).** This record previously asserted that the only governing ceiling was a relative one from RPIP-15 — "in any given award period, no more than 50% of the awarded RPL SHALL go to retroactive awards". That rule is not in force and has not been for about three years. RPIP-26, whose vote passed on 2023-08-18, states: "This RPIP supercedes RPIP-18: it removes the 50% retrospective award cap." RPIP-15, RPIP-18 and RPIP-26 now all carry the banner "🛑 This RPIP has been marked obsolete and is no longer in force"; the document currently in force is RPIP-40 (Status: Final, vote passed 2024-03-28), which restates the removal and sets no retrospective cap of its own. The only relative ceiling RPIP-40 does cite is at committee level, not track level — "RPIP-10 sets aside 30% of the pDAO budget for Grants and Bounties" — which sizes the whole GMC treasury shared by the grants, bounty and retrospective tracks. The round's own total awarded amount is never published in advance, and Round 38, the most recent published results, recorded no retrospective applications at all. This record therefore carries no `fundingInfo` — now because nothing published sizes this track, not because of a superseded cap.

opportunities.title: Safe Ecosystem Foundation Grants
opportunities.description:
The Safe Ecosystem Foundation supports builders, researchers and communities advancing the adoption and security of smart account infrastructure. Its programs are governed by SafeDAO and powered by the SAFE token.

**What it funds (six areas):**
- **Protocol & Infrastructure** — core smart account improvements, module development, standards work (e.g. ERC-4337), and interoperability.
- **Security** — audits, formal verification, vulnerability research, and defensive tooling that hardens the Safe stack.
- **Developer Tooling & SDKs** — libraries, SDKs, APIs and integrations that make it easier to build on Safe.
- **Research** — academic and applied research on account abstraction, governance, key management and related topics.
- **Ecosystem Growth** — educational content, documentation, community events and adoption campaigns.
- **Applications** — products and services built on Safe that demonstrate novel use cases for smart accounts.

**Spontaneous Grants — the active rolling track.** "The Foundation accepts unsolicited grant proposals on a rolling basis. If you are building something that advances the Safe ecosystem and need financial support, we want to hear from you." Process:
1. Submit your proposal by email to grants@safefoundation.org.
2. Include: project description, scope & milestones, budget breakdown, team background, and expected impact.
3. The Foundation reviews proposals internally. **Expect an initial reply within 4 weeks.**
4. Approved grants are paid in milestones tied to deliverables.

No award range is published for the Spontaneous Grants track.

**Other initiatives (for context, not the rolling track):** the SafeDAO Grants Program Wave 1 is concluded (Aug 2023 - Jan 2024; 120 applications, 21 grants awarded, ~$500K deployed across Build, Growth, Research and Govern). SafeDAO OBRA, an outcomes-based allocation model of approximately $1.3M in stablecoins, is temporarily paused. The Safe smart account bug bounty is ongoing and separate, with rewards up to $1,000,000 for High severity, up to $50,000 for Medium and up to $10,000 for Low; six bounties worth $41,500 have been paid to date. Hackathon sponsorship is ongoing, with 100+ winner teams and $250K in prizes distributed.

The Foundation published no announcement post for the grants page, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the program was publicly visible by 11 March 2026, the first capture of the Foundation homepage that links /grants — the 8 January and 1 February 2026 captures carry no such link — and the grants page itself is first captured 19 April 2026.

**The missing number here is deliberate, and the same page proves it.** Spontaneous Grants is the only initiative on the Foundation's grants page with no figure attached — every other one is sized right there, as quoted above. The track runs the other way round: the applicant supplies the budget, in the "budget breakdown" the submission asks for, so there is no envelope for the Foundation to publish. Nor is one waiting in governance. SEP 54 (July 2025) established "a temporary funding pause on all resource allocation initiatives of SafeDAO", during which "the Foundation will assess and redesign the funding mechanisms based on learnings from previous approaches", and no replacement envelope has been published since; the forum has never discussed this track at all.

opportunities.title: Scroll Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for Scroll, the EVM-compatible zk-Rollup scaling Ethereum, covering both the blockchain/DLT layer and the bridge and rollup smart contracts, hosted on Sherlock.

The Sherlock listing shows the program live since 2 April 2026, with a maximum reward of $250,000. Critical blockchain/DLT findings pay $20,000-$250,000, scaled linearly by the program's published "risk ratio" — funds at risk divided by Scroll's market cap, the latter averaged between CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko at submission time — with the $20,000 floor paid "in order to incentivize security researchers against withholding on a bug report". Critical smart-contract findings pay 10% of the funds directly affected, with a $50,000 minimum and the same $250,000 cap; High findings pay 100% of the funds affected up to $20,000; Medium smart-contract findings pay a flat $5,000. Repeatable attacks decay: subsequent attacks are counted at a 25% reduction per hour (blockchain/DLT) or per 300 blocks (smart contracts) where the vulnerable component cannot be paused or upgraded.

One reading note: the brief's smart-contract reward table headlines Critical at "20,000 USD - 250,000 USD", while its own reward-calculation section sets the smart-contract Critical minimum at $50,000. The calculation section is the more specific rule and the record follows it; the $20,000 floor belongs to the blockchain/DLT tier.

The program text carries `utm_source=immunefi` on its audit-report links — it migrated from Scroll's former Immunefi listing, which advertised a $1,000,000 maximum. The Sherlock program, with its $250,000 maximum, is the current one, and this record describes it rather than the retired listing.

fundingDetails.severityScheme: The programme's own severity definitions published in the Sherlock brief (Critical: definite significant loss or >1-year freeze of funds; High: considerable direct loss, >1% and >$10; Medium: constrained or conditional loss, >0.01% and >$10)

opportunities.prerequisites: A coded proof of concept with instructions to run it is required with every report. Where the team can pause or upgrade against an exploit, potential damage is assessed over a 1-hour exploit period. The scope tab's repository link may point at an older commit; the newest commit of the codebase is the one to audit. Unfixed issues already named in the published audit reports are ineligible.

Rewards are denominated in USD and paid in USDC. Prior audits linked from the brief: Trail of Bits (zkTrie, L2geth, EIP-4844 blob support, Euclid upgrade phases 1-2), OpenZeppelin (twelve reviews from Phase 1 through Batch Token Bridge) and Zellic (v1, v2, Lido Gateway). opportunities.title: SSV Grants Program
opportunities.description:
The ssv.network Grants Program, **led by the SSV Foundation**, funds teams building services for the SSV Network ecosystem, with the intent of promoting and accelerating development and innovation by building on top of ssv.network. The program is presented publicly under the headline "$5M Grants Program" and is community-led.

**Grant categories:**
- **Open Grants** — supporting unique use cases for SSV across the ecosystem.
- **Strategic Partnerships** — partnerships to develop critical components like performance data, monitoring tools and integrations.
- **Performance and Metadata Providers** — reliable performance and metadata services for the SSV ecosystem.
- **Alerting & Monitoring Solutions** — tools for real-time network monitoring and alerting.
- **Alternative Client Implementations** — different client software to improve network resilience and diversification.
- **Staking Integrations** — partnering with major staking protocols to enhance ecosystem interoperability.
- **Developer Tools** — tools that assist developers building on the SSV network.
- **Bug Bounties** — run separately as a $1M program powered by Immunefi.
- **Micro Grants** — smaller grants for impactful contributions, often awarded retroactively, honouring those who significantly contributed to the community and the project in unforeseen ways. Anyone in the community can be awarded one or suggest a candidate.

**Process:** applications are reviewed on a rolling basis by the **Grants Committee**, which votes on approval and communicates the decision to the applicant. Accepted grant applications are published on the ssv.network forum. Milestone completion is then tracked closely together with the Grants Committee. All grantees must sign agreements with the SSV Foundation and complete **KYC/KYB**.

Grant sizes are negotiated per application rather than published as a range; the program's own showcase cites SSVScan (by DragonStake and Polkastats) as having received a **$300k** grant. Program contact: matthias@ssv.network.

The SSV Foundation published no announcement date, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the program's own public application page was publicly visible by 25 August 2022, its first capture. The SSV DAO forum proposal that created the program ("Eco-system Grant Program") was posted 12 April 2022.

opportunities.title: Starknet Bug Bounty (Blockchain/DLT)
opportunities.description:
Bug bounty for the Starknet validity-rollup's core stack — the Starknet OS written in Cairo, the sequencer, the L1 core contracts in Solidity and the Cairo common library — hosted on HackenProof and triaged by the platform.

The HackenProof listing shows the program live since 1 July 2026 with a listed end date of 30 September 2026 — a bounded submission window rather than an open-ended one, which the deadline on this record carries — and $11,000 paid across 80 submissions from 36 hackers in its first weeks; its catalogue entry reports a last update on 10 August 2026. Critical findings pay from a $15,000 floor up to $250,000, computed as 10% of the funds directly affected — scaled by the ratio of funds at risk across all affected projects on the chain to Starknet's market cap, averaged between CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko at submission time. High findings — total network shutdown or an unintended chain split — pay a fixed $10,000, and medium findings, explicitly including STWO verifier soundness bugs, a fixed $2,500. Low findings are listed but carry no reward, which is why no low tier appears in this record's table.

The program is one of a family of three Starknet listings launched on HackenProof the same day — the sibling "Starknet Web & SC" program covers the StarkGate bridge contracts and starkgate.starknet.io, and "Starknet Staking" advertises up to $100,000. This record carries the flagship Blockchain/DLT program, whose $250,000 ceiling is the family's largest.

AI-generated reports without a runnable proof of concept are rejected, and simultaneous submission of the same finding to other platforms is prohibited. Malicious-operator exploits are out of scope until the network decentralizes.

Out of scope: malicious-operator exploits until decentralization. The programme page does not state the settlement asset, so none is claimed here. Response SLAs published on the listing: first response 3 business days, triage 3, reward 3, resolution 14. Sibling programs launched the same day: Starknet Web & SC (StarkGate bridge, smart-contract critical $15,000-$250,000, web critical $5,000-$10,000): https://hackenproof.com/programs/starknet-web-and-sc — Starknet Staking (up to $100,000): https://hackenproof.com/programs/starknet-staking. opportunities.title: Starknet Growth Grants
opportunities.description:
The Starknet Growth Grants Program provides non-dilutive funding to later-stage teams actively growing the Starknet ecosystem. The Foundation's grants overview publishes the band as **$25K to $1M STRK** — USD-denominated and paid in STRK — with the Growth Grants page itself stating 'Teams can receive up to $1M in funding'.

Growth Grants are organised into six categories, each with its own pre-filtered intake form: **Innovation Grants** (next-generation Starknet applications, infrastructure and protocols), **Ecosystem Integration Grants** (bridging Starknet with other networks and expanding interoperability), **Content & Creator Grants** (stories that educate and inspire Starknet users, or apps that make creators the owners of their own stories), **'The Next Billion'™ Grants** (intuitive, secure, accessible experiences that onboard the next billion users without compromising self-custody), **Bitcoin Builder Grant** (applications and infrastructure unlocking cross-chain possibilities between Starknet and Bitcoin), and **Other Grants**.

Intake is rolling with a target response of about one month. The process runs in six stages: (1) **Application** via the grants submission form, presenting a clear plan for using the grant within the next three months; (2) **Internal evaluation** by an internal committee against potential impact, innovation, milestones, community engagement, track record and embeddedness with the Starknet ecosystem; (3) **Interviews** — Growth applicants go through a rigorous interview process to understand their goals and requirements in the ecosystem; (4) **Results** communicated within approximately one month; (5) **Onboarding** after completing KYC and signing a grant agreement; (6) **Post-grant check-in** at three months, with grantees sharing regular updates such as blog posts, videos and AMAs.

The Starknet Foundation retains sole discretion over recipients and reserves the right to modify, amend or discontinue its grant programmes at any time without notice.

Growth Grants were announced by the Starknet Foundation on 17 September 2024 — "we are excited to announce the launch of Growth Grants! Growth Grants will provide up to $1M" — and the program page was first captured the same day.

Teams are required to have a compelling and reliable product and to go through a rigorous review process including interviews. The grants overview additionally frames the stage bar as: later stage, production-grade product maturity, go-to-market required. Related Seed Grants FAQ guidance for stepping up to Growth: you have received a seed grant and performed exceptionally well, you have a product that is live, production grade and reliable, and your project fits within a Request for Proposals. opportunities.title: Starknet Seed Grants
opportunities.description:
The Starknet Seed Grants Program provides up to $25,000 in non-dilutive funding to early-stage teams building in the Starknet ecosystem. Amounts are quoted in US dollars and paid out in STRK: the Starknet Foundation's own FAQ answers 'What currency are grants paid in?' with 'Seed Grants are paid out in STRK.'

Intake is continuous — 'you can apply for Seed Grants on an ongoing basis', with applications reviewed in rounds and no application deadlines. The Foundation targets a response in about one month (roughly four weeks).

Application process, in the Foundation's own five stages: (1) **Application** — apply via the grants submission form; all teams should present a clear plan detailing how the grant will be used within the next three months. (2) **Internal evaluation** — an internal committee assesses each application on potential impact, innovation, milestones, community engagement and track record, and embeddedness with the Starknet ecosystem. (3) **Results** — decisions communicated in approximately four weeks; rejected applicants are also notified. (4) **Onboarding** — after completing KYC/KYB and signing a grant agreement, funds are released. (5) **Post-grant check-in** — after three months the Foundation checks in with grantees to assess results, with grantees expected to share regular updates such as blog posts, videos and AMAs.

Applications are confidential and shared only with the Starknet Foundation and StarkWare teams. Repeat applications are permitted, and teams that have previously received StarkWare or Starknet Foundation funding may apply. Teams needing more than $25,000 are directed to the Growth Grants Program.

Seed Grants were announced by the Starknet Foundation on 6 May 2024, in the post "Announcing the Seed Grant Program".

opportunities.title: Starknet x Denarii Labs Accelerator
opportunities.description:
"Denarii Labs is partnering with the Starknet ecosystem to invest in and accelerate startups building on Ethereum's most powerful ZK-Rollup. From DeFi and gaming to AI agents and infrastructure — build with unlimited scale, low costs, and Ethereum-grade security." Denarii Labs describes itself as "a premier tokenomics accelerator and consulting agency backed by RedBeard Ventures".

Headline terms as published: Start Date Q3 2026 · Duration 12 Weeks · Format Remote · Investment $100K. From the FAQ: "Each project receives $100K in initial investment. Based on progress, projects may receive an additional $200K in follow-on funding. Terms are founder-friendly, structured as a SAFE or token warrant."

Program structure, four phases over 12 weeks: Weeks 1–2 Foundation & Mentoring (1-on-1 mentor matching, project assessment and gap analysis, token model framework selection, cohort kickoff); Weeks 3–6 Tokenomics Deep Dive (token supply and emission modeling, utility and demand driver design, distribution and vesting strategy, governance framework); Weeks 7–10 Execution & GTM (go-to-market strategy, community and narrative building, exchange listing prep, legal and compliance review); Weeks 11–12 Demo Day & Beyond (investor pitch preparation, Demo Day presentation, follow-on funding introductions, alumni network onboarding).

What participants get: "$100K investment from Denarii Labs; Direct access to the Starknet ecosystem; Weekly 1-on-1 sessions with tokenomics experts; Legal advisory for token models and compliance; Introductions to VCs, exchanges, and market makers; Post-program alumni network and continued advisory support."

Target projects, four buckets: DeFi & Financial Infrastructure (AMMs, DEXs and aggregators; lending, borrowing and yield protocols; perpetuals and structured products; stablecoin and synthetic asset platforms); Gaming & Onchain Worlds (fully onchain games using Dojo; in-game economies and asset systems; autonomous worlds and composable game logic; creator economy and digital collectibles); AI Agents & Verifiable Compute (verifiable AI inference and agent frameworks; provable ML model execution; tamper-proof data pipelines; autonomous onchain agents); Infrastructure & Tooling (Cairo developer tools and libraries; block explorers, indexers and APIs; bridges, oracles and cross-chain infra; SN Stack appchain tooling).

Admission and commitment, from the FAQ: teams need not already be building on Starknet ("We welcome teams exploring Starknet as well as those already building with Cairo") and need not know Cairo ("Cairo experience is helpful but not required"); the program is fully remote over 12 weeks with an expected "10–15 hours per week for mentor sessions, workshops, cohort calls, and independent work on tokenomics deliverables"; and "We typically accept 8–12 projects per cohort. We look for strong founding teams with a clear vision, a genuine need for tokenomics expertise, and a product with real traction or a compelling roadmap."

As of 2026-08-11 the page carries an "Applications Open" badge and live "Apply Now" buttons routing to the Airtable form; no application deadline is published.

The Starknet track was first announced in Denarii Labs' weekly newsletter of 5 March 2026 — "Join our current accelerator alongside Canton and Starknet". opportunities.title: Strata Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling smart-contract bug bounty for Strata, the Ethereum tranching protocol splitting yield into Junior and Senior tranches through a CDO-style architecture, hosted on Immunefi and live since 1 October 2025.

The program page shows last updated 8 July 2026, with a maximum reward of $250,000 for a critical finding, calculated as 10% of the funds directly affected with a $10,000 floor. The scope is 11 smart-contract assets on Ethereum — tranche and cooldown contracts, exit-fee governance and routing helpers. The PoC bar is unusually specific: submissions must reflect a deployable protocol state with each tranche seeded with at least 10 assets, and findings that depend on a tranche sitting at the protocol's one-asset accounting floor are closed as invalid.

opportunities.title: Taiko Grants (2025 Grant Fund)
opportunities.description:
Taiko Grants is an ongoing grant fund announced on 19 March 2025 as 'Taiko Grant Cycle 3: $25M to Support Community Builders and Partners' — the Taiko 2025 Grant Fund, 'with a total of $25 million in funding'. The figure is quoted in US dollars only; the page nowhere denominates the fund in TAIKO tokens, so the record's currency is USD.

The fund supports developers, researchers and builders working on groundbreaking ideas in DeFi, AI, RWA, SocialFi, Gaming and beyond. Six grant tracks are published — DeFi (lending, borrowing, trading and other financial applications), AI (blockchain + artificial intelligence), RWA (tokenising and managing real-world assets), SocialFi (social networks with financial features), Gaming (gaming applications, NFT projects and metaverse experiences), and Other (projects leveraging Taiko's strengths such as Ethereum-equivalence, based design and permissionless proposing/proving) — and each is marked 'Applications open on an ongoing basis'.

As of 2026-08-11 the program page is live and unchanged in posture: 'The Grants Council will review applications on a rolling basis and reach out to applicants', the Airtable intake form returns HTTP 200, and no successor cycle or closure notice is published. The site footer reads '© 2026 Taiko Foundation'. No per-grant amount range is published anywhere on the page.

Program conditions: unless agreed otherwise, all smart contracts and frontend code must be open-sourced from the project's inception; projects involving dApps must choose Taiko as one of their first platforms (they may also deploy and integrate on other L1/L2/L3s); grantees and Taiko must establish a formal legal agreement detailing both parties' expectations and responsibilities; all grantees undergo KYC/KYB checks; and awardees may not disclose the grant — including the number of vested or received tokens — until Taiko has announced it. Grantees may hold grants from other projects concurrently provided all other requirements are met. Taiko also runs a separate ongoing initiative, Taiko Takeoff (takeoff.taiko.xyz).

opportunities.title: The Graph Grants Program
opportunities.description:
**⚠️ Applications are paused.** On 6 July 2026 The Graph Foundation announced on its official forum: "The Graph Foundation is pausing applications to the Grants Program. Over the years, the Grants Program has supported grantees across the ecosystem with millions of dollars in funding. In recent months, we made the decision to pause the Grants Program to reassess our ecosystem strategic priorities." No reopening date has been announced.

Note that the public grants page at thegraph.com/grants and its Typeform application link were both still reachable when checked on 2026-08-11 and had not been updated to reflect the pause, so page liveness alone is not evidence that intake is open.

**Program as documented.** The Graph grants program is a gateway for contributing to web3, awarding grants for protocol, tooling, subgraph and dapp development, and growth initiatives, distributed from the community treasury. It is overseen by **The Graph Foundation and The Graph Council**, with support from community domain experts and core contributors. Grants go to individuals, projects and initiatives that are open source and contribute to the growth of The Graph ecosystem — "You don't have to be technical to receive a grant!"

**Four categories:**
- **Protocol** — advance The Graph Network with R&D on smart contracts, network operations, Graph Node, cryptography and other core development.
- **Tooling** — subgraph and Indexer tooling to improve developer experience, expand features, help users engage with the network and simplify network operations.
- **Data Services** — create and use subgraphs and Substreams to build new data services, dapps and dashboards.
- **Community** — grow the network, subgraph usage and web3 knowledge through education, content, events and developer support.

Grants have been awarded in numbered waves; the public grantee directory lists 100 grantees. The separate RFP track shows "There are no open RFPs at this time".

**Scale:** The Graph Foundation's 2025 Annual Grants Report states lifetime grant funding exceeding **$16.8M**. In 2025 the program funded five R&D teams delivering Horizon, advanced the Token API to production readiness, integrated AI-native tooling via Subgraph MCP, and expanded multi-chain coverage.

The program was announced on 11 December 2020, alongside the inaugural Graph Council: "Announcing The Graph Council members and The Graph Grants Program to support ecosystem development", with the first grants estimated for Q1 2021.

opportunities.title: Unichain Grants
opportunities.description:
**Scope of this record: the Unichain grants track only.** The Uniswap Foundation's Build on Uniswap page lists two grant intakes as separate rows with separate forms. This record is the narrow one — "Unichain grants — Unichain DeFi projects with $250K+ TVL and infrastructure projects can apply for product and GTM support, with up to $7.5K in grants funding" — and it carries that row's form and its $7,500 ceiling. The Foundation also runs a broad programme on the same page — "Uniswap Foundation grants — The Uniswap Foundation Grants program funds teams building across the Uniswap ecosystem — protocols, tooling, research, governance, and community. We support projects at any stage, from early experiments to production systems ready to scale" — which takes a different form and publishes no ceiling. That programme is NOT this record: it is not represented in this corpus, and the $7,500 here must not be read as its award ceiling. Verified live 2026-08-13.

The context below describes the Foundation's grant-making as a whole, because the Unichain track is administered inside it and the Foundation publishes its terms once, for both. The Uniswap Foundation funds work across the Uniswap Protocol and Unichain in five focus areas it publishes as: **Developers** (onboarding new developers to build on the Uniswap Protocol and supporting them through the development lifecycle), **Infrastructure** (new core infrastructure and growth strategies), **Governance** (empowering Uniswap governance to support protocol growth and sustain itself), **Research** (seeding DeFi research and its practical implementations), and **Security** (protecting the Protocol's users through investments into security). Its grants page groups the funded portfolio under Ecosystem, Research, Security and Governance.

**Payment currency and mechanics:** the Foundation's FAQ states that "Grant payments are currently made in fiat USD or USDC." During the Selection phase a team member works with the applicant to outline grant milestones, each tied to clear deliverables and to a portion of the overall payment; **grants typically have 2-5 milestones**, defined in the contract executed on approval. The initial payment is disbursed after KYC and contract signature, and subsequent payments on completion of each milestone. Every grantee is assigned a point person for 1-1 support and milestone check-ins.

Representative funded work includes the Uniswap Hook Incubator (Atrium Academy, 1,200+ applicants and 400+ developers onboarded), the OpenZeppelin v4 Hooks Library, the Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (Areta), v4 audits (OpenZeppelin, Trail of Bits, Cantina/Spearbit, ABDK, Certora), Unichain infrastructure and DeFi protocol onboarding support, the Protocol Grants Program (Auditless), Doppler (Whetstone), TLDR, and governance work with Agora, Blockful and Butter.

**Intake state (re-checked 2026-08-13): open.** The Foundation's current Build on Uniswap page carries a "Unichain grants" entry reading "Unichain DeFi projects with $250K+ TVL and infrastructure projects can apply for product and GTM support, with up to $7.5K in grants funding", and links exactly the form this record carries as its `applicationUrl`; that form returns HTTP 200 with no closure markers. The separate grants page at uniswapfoundation.org/grants is a funded-portfolio and impact view rather than an intake: it carries no application form and no occurrence of "apply", "application", "submit" or "intake" anywhere in its markup, and /grants/apply and /apply both return HTTP 404. Nothing on any Foundation page or on gov.uniswap.org announces a closure, pause or sunset. No deadline is published; applications are read as they arrive.

Unichain Developer Grants were announced by the Uniswap Foundation on 14 October 2024, in the post "Introducing Unichain Developer Grants".

**Award ceiling, and why no envelope is recorded.** The only Unichain-attributed figure the Foundation publishes is the per-grant ceiling quoted above — "up to $7.5K in grants funding", re-verified live on the Build on Uniswap page on 2026-08-12 — and it is recorded here as `fundingInfo.maxAward` of 7,500 USD. It is a maximum award and not a programme budget, so no budget is recorded: the Foundation publishes no Unichain-earmarked envelope. The number that does exist is foundation-wide: the Uniswap Unleashed proposal, executed on-chain in March 2025, requested "an investment of $95.4M into the UF grants budget, and $25.1M to fund operations, for the next 2 years", with "projected grants budgets for 2025 and 2026 [of] $57.9M and $41.5M respectively" — across Ecosystem, Research, Security and Governance, and across both Uniswap protocol and Unichain work. Putting it on this record would assert an attribution the Foundation never made. The same proposal names the Unichain-specific programs (Developer Growth Programs, a Unichain Infrastructure Allocation, a Unichain DeFi Partner Allocation, Unigames) without sizing any of them; the per-program breakdown exists only inside an embedded chart image. The sibling $45M is liquidity incentives, not grants.

The one publication that might have carried a Unichain-earmarked figure — the original announcement on Mirror — is unrecoverable: Mirror migrated to Paragraph, the URL now serves that platform's own homepage and no capture of the post exists. The Foundation's blog post announcing the program, referenced above, is the live equivalent and carries no figure.

opportunities.title: Usual Protocol Bug Bounty
opportunities.description:
Rolling bug bounty for the Usual Protocol — issuer of **USD0**, a stablecoin fully collateralized by real-world assets — covering the protocol's smart contracts deployed on Ethereum mainnet, hosted on Sherlock.

The Sherlock listing shows the program live since 8 April 2025, with a maximum reward of $16,000,000 for a critical finding, capped at 10% of funds at risk at the time of submission. High and Medium findings are paid at Usual Labs' discretion — the program's own words: "High severity payouts will be determined case-by-case by Usual Labs (amount will reflect the impact)" — and Low or Informational issues are not eligible for rewards. Severity and validity are judged by Sherlock's security team, not by Usual Labs.

**Scope splits by severity ceiling.** The core contracts (`USD0`, `USD0PP`, `DaoCollateral`, `RegistryAccess`, `RegistryContract`, `SwapperEngine`, `ClassicalOracle`, `TokenMapping`) form the Critical tier; all other deployed Usual contracts (`Usual.sol`, `EulerOracle`, `UsualX`, the Distribution module, `UsualUSDtB`, `UsualM`) are eligible for High or Medium only. Euler-vault-related code is explicitly referred to a separate bounty on Cantina rather than covered here.

One reading note on chain scope: the brief's Scope section states "Ethereum Mainnet only. (Smart contracts on any other networks or testnets are out-of-scope.)", while its Additional Context section lists "Ethereum, Arbitrum" as chains in scope. The Scope section is the operative one — only contracts currently deployed on mainnet are in scope — and the record follows it.

opportunities.title: World Foundation Scale Track Mini App Grant
opportunities.description:
The Scale Track is one of two active Mini App grant tracks in the World Foundation Grants program, funded from a pool of **50M WLD** — a token quantity, not a dollar figure. The Foundation describes it as 'Scale Track Grant — supercharge a live Mini App with real users and grow 10×', for live Mini Apps that are already being used by real, verified humans and need capital to grow faster. It looks for strong usage or retention data, a clear go-to-market strategy, and a plan to grow 10× or more from where the product is now.

Grants are available on a rolling basis — 'apply any time' — and the Foundation states its team will review proposals promptly. No per-track award size is published on world.org/grants. The Scale Track Airtable intake form was verified live (HTTP 200) on 2026-08-11.

The grants program sits alongside a rolling, usage-based **Developer Rewards** pilot: a $300K USD pool paid in WLD across its first three months (launched 27 Mar 2025), distributed monthly pro-rata to qualifying Mini Apps based on verified-human usage metrics, open to any Mini App live in World App that meets the program T&Cs. Rewards can be stacked on top of Spark or Scale funding, turning usage into a recurring revenue stream.

The World Foundation notes it may, at its discretion, choose to make grants directly in USDC or a similar stablecoin rather than in WLD, for commercial and regulatory reasons. Grant recipients are responsible for any tax payable in their home jurisdiction.

Historic context published by the Foundation: Wave 0 (Q1 2024) funded 28 projects with approximately 800K WLD total awarded, and Wave 1 (Q3 2024) funded 16 projects with approximately 289K WLD total awarded, for community events and RFPs.

**No per-track envelope is recorded.** world.org/grants publishes exactly one funding figure — a stats tile reading "50M WLD for World Grants", which occurs once on the page — and it sizes the grants programme as a whole rather than this track. That same page lists three programmes under it: Spark Track, Scale Track and the Developer Rewards pilot described above, so the envelope is broader than the two Mini App tracks even taken together. Four places were checked on 2026-08-13 for a per-track split and none publishes one: world.org/grants itself; world.org/community-grants, which serves the same page; the World developer documentation at docs.world.org/world-chain/developers/grants, which publishes no funding figures at all; and docs.world.org/mini-apps/more/grants, which returns HTTP 404. The programme is described publicly only at envelope level — "up to 50M WLD" for Mini Apps built on World Chain. This record therefore carries no `fundingInfo`. The 50M WLD is real and is stated above, but attaching it to the Scale Track alone would assert a split the Foundation has not published, and attaching it to both tracks would count one pool twice.

The Foundation published no announcement post for the track, so `postedAt` is an archival bound: the Scale Track was publicly visible by 14 May 2025, the first capture of world.org/grants, which already lists it with its apply button. The February 2025 developer-docs grants page still described only "Fast Grants" and "Foundation Grants", so this track framing is newer than that.

opportunities.title: Filecoin ProPGF Batch 1
opportunities.description:
**Concluded.** Filecoin ProPGF Batch 1 was the first round of the Filecoin ProPGF program — milestone-based funding for teams building foundational infrastructure, developer tooling and essential services for the Filecoin ecosystem.

**$3.68M awarded, not budgeted.** The figure this program is usually described by is the amount AWARDED, and this record says so: the results post reads "A total of $3.68M in funding has been allocated to 14 teams" over a pull-out stat of "$3,681,800 allocated", and the programme's own retrospective, *Reflections from ProPGF Batch 1* (17 October 2025), restates it as "we reviewed 38 applications, shortlisted 23, and funded 14 teams with a total of $3.68 million". Every published phrasing is retrospective. (Until 2026-08-13 this record put a differently-worded sentence in quotation marks and attributed it to "a later Foundation post". That sentence is not findable verbatim on any published page, and the attribution was wrong twice over: the wording above is the published one, and ProPGF is a Protocol Labs programme — the results post states that "Protocol Labs' Filecoin Public Goods Funding (PGF) programs support projects that strengthen the Filecoin ecosystem" — not a Filecoin Foundation one, the Foundation being a separate entity.) No Batch 1 pool was ever pre-announced — unlike the Batch 2 General Track, whose $4M ceiling was announced up front — so this record carries `allocated` and deliberately no `budget`. Awards ran from $25,000 to $500,000 per project and settle in USDC, but no eligibility minimum or maximum was ever published, so no award range is recorded either.

**One figure that does not match, and why the announcement's is used.** The program's own payout ledger reports 3,741,800 for the same 14 grants — roughly $60,000 more, from post-announcement adjustments — and carries an explicit data-quality note that its Batch 1 records were entered retrospectively and in bulk rather than captured in real time. The announced total is the published one and is what this record carries; the two should not be mixed.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is 25 March 2025, the date of the *Introducing FIL ProPGF* post, which opened the first call — "Formal applications open the week of March 31st". That first call is what the ecosystem later named Batch 1; no separate Batch 1 announcement was ever published, so this is the earliest dated public notice of the round.

**Eligibility, corrected 2026-08-13.** This record previously carried the sentence "Not open to all applicants — the program invites or pre-selects participants." That is an upstream intake flag rendered as prose, and it contradicted this record's own documented application window. ProPGF's General Track rounds are open calls decided by a selection committee; the programme's Pods Track, which is a separate record, is the part of ProPGF that is not open.

**No application deadline is recorded.** The only window this round ever published is the roadmap in that same post — "Formal applications open the week of March 31st", "Application period closes (Late April)" — which names no date. Until 2026-08-13 this record carried a fixed application deadline of 2025-10-01, which came from the upstream registry snapshot's operational end date rather than from the funder, and which postdated the round's own results post of 11 August 2025 by seven weeks — on its face, applications closing after the winners were announced. It has been removed rather than replaced with a guess, because "Late April" is not a date.
opportunities.summary: The first round of Filecoin's ProPGF public-goods program: $3,681,800 awarded to 14 teams building Filecoin infrastructure, developer tooling and essential services, paid against milestones. The round is closed and its results are published.
opportunities.eligibility: Open application, competitively selected. The round ran a public call — the opening announcement scheduled "Formal applications open the week of March 31st" with an "Application period closes (Late April)" — and the funder reports 38 applications received, 23 shortlisted and 14 funded. Selection sat with a committee: the programme "incorporates a selection committee composed of subject matter experts from the Filecoin ecosystem", 12 members for this round, with Snapshot used for public visibility of the review and Questbook for grant management. Nothing published gated who could apply; the shortlist was the filter. Grants are milestone-based and settle in USDC.

opportunities.title: Localism Mini Grant Round 01 | Colombia
opportunities.description:
This program funds ReFi Colombia local nodes to execute place based regenerative and community onboarding activities across Colombia.

Through an open local round, up to 5 nodes *(either existing or proposed new nodes)* will be selected and awarded between $750 and $2,000 each. Funding decisions will be based on proposal quality, node history and previous activities, consistency of participation in ReFi Colombia meetings and initiatives, collaboration within the ReFi Colombia and wider ReFiDAO network, and alignment with ReFi Colombia’s values, mission, and rules.

New node activations are also eligible. These will be evaluated using adapted criteria, including prior participation in activities organized by existing nodes, engagement in the ReFi Colombia Telegram community and social media channels, the background and experience of the proposed team, and demonstrated commitment to ReFi Colombia’s values, mission, and internal rules.

Supported activities include reforestation, environmental restoration, ReFi-focused educational workshops, cleanup actions, mindfulness and community well being initiatives, and Web3 onboarding through these activities. The program prioritizes local leadership, continuity, expansion potential, and transparent allocation, enabling nodes to scale activities according to their real on-the-ground capacity while strengthening the national ReFi Colombia network.

**Announcement date not established.** The organisers' own site no longer resolves, the round was promoted through a chat group with no public archive, and no dated announcement or usable capture survives. `postedAt` is therefore absent rather than a guess.

opportunities.title: ProPGF Batch 2 - Pods Track
opportunities.description:
The Pods Track is a coordination track designed to help Filecoin teams organize around clear user outcomes and move faster toward product–market fit (PMF).

Instead of funding isolated projects, the Pods Track supports small, focused pods (cross-functional where possible) that are accountable for shipping a defined scope, validating user needs, and contributing to Filecoin’s 2026 ecosystem goals. Pods are expected to operate like product teams: aligning on a problem, testing assumptions, delivering milestones, and reporting progress through measurable adoption and performance metrics.

**What was allocated, and how that number was arrived at.** No Pods Track pool was ever published: the ProPGF blog announces and reports only the Batch 2 General Track — a $4M round that allocated $3,220,200 across 16 projects — and the Pods Track has no announcement, no results post and no published total anywhere. What the program does publish is per-pod, in its own financials ledger: Filecoin Onchain Cloud 466,000, the Large Data Onboarding Pod 147,630, and the Web2 Object Storage Pod 267,344. The 880,974 USD on this record is those three figures summed from that ledger and nothing else — a sum of the program's own per-grant allocations, not a funder-published program total, and not a budget. It is Pods-Track-only and deliberately excludes the General Track, which is a separate record with its own budget and its own allocation. Two of the three grants settle in USDC and the third's milestones are dollar-denominated, which is what denominates the record.

**Announcement date not established.** Neither Filecoin nor the ProPGF team published a post announcing this track — the Batch 2 announcements name the General Track only — and no archived page carries an earlier dated notice of it. `postedAt` is therefore absent rather than a guess.

opportunities.title: Optimism Season 9 — Audit Grants
opportunities.description:
**Discontinued.** Audit Grants were the Developer Advisory Board's (DAB) grant track under the Optimism Collective's Governance Fund. The DAB subsidised third-party smart-contract security audits for teams building on the Superchain; projects did not apply directly but worked with whitelisted Audit Service Providers (ASPs), who applied for the grant on the project's behalf.

**Season 9 window.** Season 9 ran from 29 January 2026 to 3 June 2026. The Grants Council closed Season 9 submissions on 20 May 2026.

**Budget.** The Developer Advisory Board's Season 9 Governance Fund mission budget was 0.98M OP (up from 949k OP in Season 8). That single budget line covered both Audit Grants and Foundation Missions — Optimism did not publish an audit-only sub-budget for Season 9.

**Process.** Audit Grant applications were reviewed on a rolling basis inside the season by the DAB's Audit Program Stewards, with a target of an initial response to every applicant within 14 days (max) of submission. Steward funding recommendations were optimistically approved by the seven voting Board members; results were published as per-cycle reports on gov.optimism.io.

**Why it is closed.** The Guide to Season 9 announced the Foundation's intent to wind down community-led capital allocation. Governance Update #12 (3 June 2026) confirmed there would be no dedicated Seasons after Season 9. On 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Foundation's Developer Advisory Board Dissolution Proposal (22.33M OP For / 198.45K Against), dissolving the board that ran this program, effective immediately. No replacement audit-grant intake has been published, and the former intake site opgrants.io still resolves over valid TLS but no longer serves the program: as of 2026-08-13 it returns HTTP 200 with a registrar parking page reading "Domain registration has expired", offering the name at auction. The `applicationUrl` on this record is that address because it is where the funder published the intake, not because anything answers for the program on it.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is the creation date of the *Season 9 Governance Fund Missions* topic on gov.optimism.io, 7 January 2026 — the post that set out the Developer Advisory Board's Season 9 mission and its 0.98M OP budget, and the first public statement of this track for the season.

opportunities.title: Optimism Season 9 — Growth Grants
opportunities.description:
**Discontinued.** Growth Grants were the Grants Council's proactive incentive-grant track under the Optimism Collective's Season 9 Governance Fund mission.

**Mission scope.** The Season 9 primary success metric was *DEX TVL for collateral-borrow pairs that exist on lending markets* (e.g. Morpho, Aave) — both assets in a liquidity pair had to be available on a lending market (e.g. a WETH/USDC DEX pool where WETH is collateral and USDC is the borrowed asset). The secondary metric was DEX trading volume per TVL for those same pairs. Impact was measured at the end of the Season by OP Labs or Open Source Observer.

**Window.** Season 9 ran 29 January 2026 to 3 June 2026; the Grants Council closed Season 9 submissions on 20 May 2026.

**Budget and outcome.** The Season 9 Grants Council budget was 3,690,000 OP (the Budget Board's proposed mission figure was 3.89M OP, down from ~6.29M OP in Season 8); 90,000 OP was returned unallocated at the end of the season. Season 9 drew 38 applications in total. Applications first passed an AI filter, then GrantNerds human review, then the Grants Council; GrantNerds reviewed 29 applications and passed 10 to the Council, of which 4 were funded, while the Council reviewed a further 19 directly and passed 8. Approved Season 9 growth grants in the final cycle ranged from 150,000 OP to 1,000,000 OP.

**Where it was submitted, and why no `applicationUrl` is recorded.** Optimism published the Season 9 intake as a Growth Grant form on its own grants platform, linked from its season page directly above "Applications Open: Feb 11th 2026 / Submissions Closes: May 20th 2026", and the season's own reports link individual submissions there. That host no longer completes a TLS handshake — there is no HTTP status at all, not even an error — and only archive captures of the form remain. An archived copy of a form is not a place to apply, so the field is left absent.

**Why it is closed.** Governance Update #12 (3 June 2026) confirmed there would be no dedicated Seasons after Season 9. On 15 July 2026 the Token House passed the Foundation's Grants Council Dissolution Proposal (22.34M OP For / 196.6K Against), effective immediately. The Foundation stated it will continue to make select strategic grants directly in pursuit of the OP Enterprise strategy, but community-led capital allocation has ended.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is the creation date of the *Season 9 Governance Fund Missions* topic on gov.optimism.io, 7 January 2026 — the post that set out the Grants Council's Season 9 mission and its 3.89M OP budget. Season missions for both councils were published in that one topic, so the Season 9 audit track in this corpus carries the same date.

opportunities.title: GEN Ukraine MicroGrant Program
opportunities.description:
The GEN Grant Program 01 enables a bioregional network of ecovillages to implement regenerative projects through Ethereum-aligned coordination and transparent on-chain micro-funding. Leveraging DAO governance, ReFi tools, and on-chain verification, the program funds solar resilience, water restoration, biodiversity monitoring, and community infrastructure to strengthen local regenerative capacity and decentralized economic resilience.

**Currency.** The 5,000 figure on this record reaches the corpus without a unit, and the unit is USD. The program states its own co-funding as "Confirmed co-funding of $5,000 is already secured through two on-chain community pools" and sizes the round it belongs to in dollars throughout — "We aim to raise a total of $20,000 for this round", split "60% - Local Micro-Grants ($12,000) / 20% - Program Operations & Coordination ($4,000)" and so on. Its funder's round rules are dollar-denominated too: a $125,000 USD matching pool with a "Grant Range: $5,000 - $20,000 per local program". The program's implementation report prices every disbursement in dollars as well. USD is recorded as the unit of account; the settlement rails are stablecoins (cUSD, USDC, USDGLO) and are not the denomination.

**Intake ran through the network, not through a form.** The program states that funding "will be distributed through Sarafu Network community pools" with application intake integrated into the coordination workspace GEN Ukraine already used, and its own timeline reads "Announcement & Intake (Jan 2026) - Publicly announce the GEN Ukraine Local Grant Program through our network channels ... Open call for proposals from 20+ ecovillages." Twelve applications were coordinated that way. No dedicated public application form was ever published — no form page, no Google Form, no Tally page, no Telegram intake — so this record carries no `applicationUrl`; the program's implementation report and GEN Ukraine's own site both point at that shared workspace rather than at a form of its own.

**Announcement date not established.** GEN Ukraine publishes no post, page or feed item announcing this round, and no archived page carries a dated notice of it. `postedAt` is therefore absent rather than a guess.

Build Agents for the Real World — Celo Hackathon V2 challenged teams to build agentic applications on Celo, an Ethereum Layer 2 designed for fast, low-cost global payments. The hackathon ran 2 March 2026 (kick-off, 5 PM GMT) to 23 March 2026 (submissions close, 9 AM GMT), with winners announced 24 March 2026 at 3 PM GMT. It carried an 8,500 USD₮ (USDT) prize pool, sponsored by CeloPG.

**Prize distribution**

- Track 1 — Best Agent on Celo: 1st 3,000 USD₮, 2nd 2,000 USD₮, 3rd 1,000 USD₮
- Track 2 — Best Agent Infra on Celo: 1st 2,000 USD₮
- Track 3 — Highest Rank in 8004scan for Celo (combinable with the other tracks): 1st 500 USD₮

**How to participate**

Register the project with a website link, demo video link, GitHub repository link(s), pitch deck link and contact info; join the Telegram group for support and announcements; tweet about the agent linking the project, the agentscan Registry agentId (not required for the Infra track) and optionally Self AI and a Molthunt registration, tagging @Celo, @CeloDevs and @CeloPG; then submit the tweet and project link through the hackathon form.

All agent frameworks were allowed — the frameworks named in the idea list were suggestions only. Judges were Luuk (CeloPG), Viral Sangani (AI Lead, Celo) and Marek (CEO of cLabs, the company that builds Celo — this record previously gave the title as "CEO, Celo"; Celo has no CEO, and the organiser's programme page is a JavaScript shell that serves no fetchable judge list, so the correction is against the public record rather than a re-read of the source). opportunities.title: Regenesis Season 1 Grants
opportunities.description:
The Regenesis Grants Program funds builders who ship. Each season targets specific needs in the Decentraland ecosystem — Season 1's themes were mobile-optimized content (Content Development domain) and AI-assisted tooling (Tech Ecosystem domain). Projects are scoped, milestone-tracked, and open source from day one, with a maximum of 90 days from approval to final delivery.

**Season 1 is closed.** The site's own FAQ states: "No — Season 1 applications closed on April 24, 2026." Season 1 ran April – July 2026: submissions opened 1 April, closed 24 April, evaluation 20 April – 1 May, projects kicked off 1–8 May, delivery deadline 31 July. Seven projects were awarded a total of $32,250; six went into active delivery through August 2026 (Flagtag $7,750; Decentraland Social $6,000, cancelled before kickoff; The Pixel Arcade $4,000; Goal Legends Arena $4,000; Doge Hunt $4,000; AdventureLand $3,500; Candy Sheep Meadow $3,000). The operator's own caveat: "This is a pilot season — we're testing the process and expect it to evolve."

**Season 2 is upcoming**, scheduled July – November 2026 with submissions opening in August 2026, close date TBD and themes to be announced. As of 2026-08-11 the site still reads "Season 2 is on the way — stay tuned for the next call for proposals", so Season 2 intake had not yet opened.

**Five-step process.** 1) Submit your proposal via the application form. 2) AI agent review — the proposal enters a structured review by specialized AI agents (Technical Feasibility, Creativity & Art, Gameplay & Mechanics, Marketing & Reach), each getting a dedicated forum thread where they post questions and clarification requests that applicants are expected to answer. 3) Human evaluation — the Regenesis Labs team reviews the AI assessments and takes the agents' recommendations into consideration when making the final funding decision. 4) Decision & kickoff — decisions are communicated within roughly one month after the submission window closes; approved projects are funded and start their 90-day build. 5) Build & deliver — payment is released against milestone checkpoints; missing two consecutive milestones may terminate the grant.

**Payment.** Up to $15,000 USD equivalent in MANA, Decentraland's native token, per project, paid against milestones.

opportunities.title: Arbitrum Open House — London
opportunities.description:
Arbitrum Open House — London is the London leg of Arbitrum's global builder programme, hosted by the Arbitrum Foundation and run on HackQuest, with the IRL component delivered in partnership with Encode Club.

It has two parts. First, the "Arbitrum Open House London: Online Buildathon" — a 3-week online build sprint (tech stack Solidity and Rust) with a total prize pool of 115,000 USDC, split across three reward pots of 70,000 / 30,000 / 15,000 USDC. Registration and submission opened 2026-03-24, registration closed 2026-06-12, submissions closed 2026-06-14, and rewards/winners were announced 2026-06-17. It drew 782 registered participants and 273 submitted projects.

Second, the IRL Founder House in London on 10–12 July 2026, 120 spots, described as offering "Direct access to and feedback from the Arbitrum Foundation, Offchain Labs, and Open House Sponsors", "Product, technical, go-to-market, and fundraising guidance", "Hands-on workshops covering the tools and infrastructure needed to build and scale on Arbitrum", "Dedicated time to build alongside high-quality teams" and "Opportunities to connect with investors, partners, and ecosystem leaders", with "$300,000 in prizes and grants across multiple tracks".

**Budget scope: this record carries the Founder House leg only (300,000).** The Arbitrum Foundation publishes 415,000 USD as the whole-programme envelope — "A total of $415K has been earmarked for OH London across its Buildathon and Founder House programs" — and its own prize breakdown splits that envelope into two disjoint pools: the Buildathon's 115,000 (Open Category 70,000 = 40,000 / 20,000 / 10,000; AI Agentic Category 15,000; Grants 30,000) and the Founder House's 300,000 (Open Category 120,000 = 60,000 / 40,000 / 20,000; Robinhood Chain Founder-in-Residence 60,000; Robinhood Chain Innovation Award 30,000; AI Agentic Category 20,000; Grants 70,000). The Foundation describes the Founder House pool as "an additional $300K" on top of the Buildathon's, confirming the pools do not overlap. The buildathon leg is recorded separately as its own opportunity ("Arbitrum Open House London: Online Buildathon", the HackQuest buildathon listing), which carries the 115,000; recording 415,000 here as well would double-count that 115,000 across the two records. The prizes and grants for both legs are jointly sponsored by the Arbitrum Foundation and the Robinhood Chain.

Open House also ran NYC (30,000 USD prize pool, 514 participants) and an APAC Mini Hackathon (4,000 USD, 232 participants); both are shown as Ended.

As of 2026-08-11 both legs are over: the HackQuest listing carries currentStatus REGISTER_CLOSE and VOTING_CLOSE with winners announced, and the Founder House dates are in the past.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is 11 March 2026, the date of the Arbitrum Foundation blog post closing the New York leg, which is where London was first named publicly: "Open House 2026 is just getting started. The program will soon expand to London and Singapore with both online and IRL activities." The dedicated London registration post is dated 14 April 2026 and announces registration, not the event.

opportunities.title: Yellow Acceleration #2
opportunities.description:
Yellow Acceleration #2 is a growth program for startups building with blockchain technologies, run by Yellow (the Layer-3 state-channel clearing network behind the Yellow SDK / NeoDAX). Intake is deliberately low-friction: the published form opens with "Thanks for your interest in building with Yellow! Whether you already have a clear idea or are still figuring things out - that's totally OK!" and asks applicants only to "express your intent to apply to the acceleration program", after which "our team will get back to you shortly."

The form collects name, email, Telegram handle, whether the applicant has a team, team/company name, a short description of the team and of what is being built, a GitHub or website link, availability to pitch online, and availability to pitch offline "during DAPPConference Berlin June 16-17" in the event of selection to the Final. It also asks applicants to confirm they have joined the Yellow Telegram community.

**Prizes.** Yellow published 25,000 USD in prizes for this wave, twice and only on its own X account: "We're accepting applications to Wave 2 of the Yellow Acceleration program … With 25k USD in prizes!" (23 April 2026) and "Applications for round 2 are open now, with 25K USD to be won + ongoing support channels." (1 May 2026). Both posts link to exactly the application form on this record, which is what ties the figure to this program. Both phrasings are pool-level ("in prizes", "to be won"), so this is the round's total rather than a per-team award: no split by place, no per-team cap, and no equity or token terms are published anywhere, so no award range is recorded.

Nothing else is published: no cohort size, cohort dates or application deadline appear on the form or on yellow.org. The other monetary figure Yellow publishes for builders belongs to a *different* programme — the Yellow Builder Program at yellow.org/build, which offers "up to $50K for your project" against four milestones (M0 Acceptance, M1 Kickoff, M2 Live, M3 Scaling) and has its own intake at forms.yellow.org/build. The two should not be conflated.

As of 2026-08-11 the acceleration form is still live and accepting responses (no closure notice, Submit button present), but the offline Final it points at — DAPP Conference Berlin, June 16–17 — has already passed, and Yellow has published no cohort roster, selection outcome or Round 3 announcement.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is 23 April 2026, the date Yellow announced this wave: "We're accepting applications to Wave 2 of the Yellow Acceleration program", linking the same intake form this record carries.

opportunities.title: Q402 Grant Program
opportunities.description:
The Q402 Grant Program supports builders developing gasless Web3 user experiences. **Awards are relay credits, not cash grants** — prepaid transaction-relay capacity on Q402's infrastructure, quoted in US dollars and in the number of transactions the credit covers.

**Tiers as published**

| Tier | Credit | Transactions | Also includes | Who it's for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seed | $500 relay credit | up to 10,000 txs | priority support, Q402 partner badge | "Early-stage projects exploring gasless and agentic UX" |
| Builder | $2,000 relay credit | up to 50,000 txs | co-marketing opportunity, direct Telegram access, custom chain configuration | "Live products scaling gasless and agent payments" |
| Ecosystem | Custom | Unlimited | custom credit pool, revenue share model, joint press release, board advisory access | "Strategic partners and infrastructure builders" |

**Application process.** Apply directly on the grant page; applications are reviewed within 3 to 5 business days. Follow-up is by email (business@quackai.ai) or Telegram. No deadline is published — intake is rolling.

**About the platform.** Q402 is gasless payment infrastructure for AI agents and Web3 apps, built by Quack AI. It lets users send stablecoins (USDC, USDT, RLUSD) without paying gas, using EIP-712 signatures and EIP-7702, and exposes payments to agents such as Claude and Codex through a single Model Context Protocol tool call. Status: Live on mainnet across BNB Chain, Ethereum, Mantle, Avalanche, Injective, X Layer, Stable, Monad, Scroll, Arbitrum, Base and Robinhood Chain.

That reading was correct on the date it was taken — the Season 2 round had closed on 30 June 2026 — and the Season 3 round opened on 12 August 2026, the day after. It is corrected here rather than left as post-snapshot drift on the record's most clickable link. Note for anyone re-checking by grepping the page source: the strings "This form is now closed" and "The form can't receive new submissions at this moment" are still present in the form platform's own bundled interface dictionary on a live form, so they are not on their own evidence of a closed form.

**Season 2 (closed).** The Season 2 Anchor Open Round ran 25 February 2026 – 30 June 2026.

**Outcome.** Anchor received 24 applications and funded 2 teams (BitGifty and TrenchVerse), each at $25,000, holding the traction bar rather than diluting criteria. $40,000 was reallocated out of Anchor mid-season on 5 May 2026 to capitalise a new Frontier pool for AI/agent-economy infrastructure, reducing Anchor's budget from $220,000 to $180,000; $130,015 was left uncommitted at season close and has been redeployed into Season 3.

**Grant terms.** One-off grants paid in USDm (the USD-pegged stablecoin Prezenti holds, obtained by converting its CELO disbursement through Mento), split 20% at project onset and 80% after agreed delivery, with KYC and a signed contract with Prezenti, and four months from contract signature to delivery. Applications moved from Charmverse to Tally Forms in May 2026 after Charmverse ceased trading; old Charmverse links are inactive.

**Stage-based grant sizes.** Stage 2 (Valora apps, Mini apps; 10K–100K est. daily transactions) ~$25k; Stage 3 (seed-stage or scaled products with traction; 100k–500k) ~$50k; Stage 4 (mature ecosystem apps; 500k+) case-by-case.

**Decision process.** The Prezenti review team scores proposals against a published rubric (alignment, open-source commitment, demo quality, team, metrics/KPIs, correct stage, demand understanding, financial plan, plus a discretionary factor) and reaches a final decision by internal consensus vote. Outcomes are typically returned around 4 weeks from submission, on a rolling basis, notified first by email to the lead applicant. 100% of rejected Season 2 applicants received tailored, rubric-tied feedback.

**Season 3.** A Season 3 plan was posted to the Celo governance forum on 23 July 2026, continuing Anchor alongside Boost and Frontier and funded by redeploying held funds rather than a new treasury draw. The round opened on 12 August 2026 and runs to 29 December 2026.

**No Season 3 envelope is recorded.** prezenti.xyz/grants publishes the round's window, its stage-based grant sizes and an estimated grant count, but no Season 3 Anchor budget and no allocated-to-date figure. The `budget` of $180,000 and `allocated` of $50,000 this record used to carry were Season 2 figures and would have misdescribed the open round, so they have been removed; both remain in the Season 2 prose above. The award range is kept because the live page still publishes it.

opportunities.title: Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (UFSF)
opportunities.description:
**Open — and not a single closed cohort.** The Uniswap Foundation Security Fund (UFSF) provides up to 100% coverage of security-audit costs for projects building in the Uniswap ecosystem, delivered through Areta's audit marketplace.

**Correction to the deadline.** The 7 May 2026 date on this record is a single monthly cut-off, not the end of the program. UFSF runs a **monthly cohort system**: applications close on the **7th of each month at 23:59 UTC**, and the application form **stays open year-round**. An application that misses a month's cut-off automatically enters the next month's cohort. The Uniswap Foundation still links this form directly from its own homepage.

**Fund size.** UFSF is a **$1M subsidy pool**, announced on the Uniswap governance forum as "a fund size of USD $1M created through a Uniswap Foundation grant" that "will subsidize up to 100% of the auditing fees of security services for eligible projects building Uniswap v4 hooks", and restated at Cohort 2 as "a $1M initiative to support security audits for projects building in the Uniswap ecosystem". That $1M is the pool across cohorts, not a per-project cap: "up to 100% of audit costs" is a coverage rule with no number attached, and no per-project ceiling is published anywhere, so this record carries a budget and no maximum award. The Foundation's grant to the operator is a different and larger figure — $1,200,000, covering the subsidy pool plus program management — and is not the fund size. **Recency caveat:** the $1M was announced at launch in October 2024 and last restated in February 2025; every monthly cohort post since, through August 2026, repeats the coverage rule without restating or topping up a fund size.

**Application limits.** Each project may apply to UFSF a maximum of 3 times in total; reapplying with materially new information, or consenting to carry an application forward into the next cohort, each counts toward that cap.

**Marketplace route.** Applicants who book an audit through the Areta marketplace are automatically considered for a retroactive subsidy in the next two cohorts, and a campaign incentive makes every 3rd project that accepts an offer on the marketplace eligible for cashback of up to $10,000 (subject to availability and terms). Applicants who are not booking an audit right now can either reapply with new information or carry the application forward.

**Compliance.** Applicants must accept the Head Agreement and Application Conditions at application time and may be required to execute the Foundation's Grant Agreement as part of a KYC/KYB process following a positive subsidy decision.

**Support channel.** Applicants coordinate through the UFSF Telegram group at https://t.me/UFSF_Applicants.

**Announcement.** `postedAt` is the creation date of the *Uniswap Foundation Security Fund Launch* topic on gov.uniswap.org, 24 October 2024 — the post that announced the fund and its $1M Uniswap Foundation grant.

opportunities.title: Devlynix Buildathon 1.0
opportunities.description:
Welcome to Devlynix Buildathon 1.0, an asynchronous, weekend-long mini-hackathon designed specifically to help you transition from watching tutorials to building practical, real-world projects.

This hackathon focuses on the "Idea-to-MVP Sprint" model. We aren't looking for perfect code; we are looking for strong problem-solving, clean design, and a solid technical approach.

# **⚠️ IMPORTANT: MANDATORY STEP**

All official announcements, squad formations, and shortlisting results will be shared EXCLUSIVELY on our WhatsApp handles. Joining both is mandatory for participation.

👉 Join our WhatsApp Channel: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VbCzGzaJpe8chzjL0w1F
👉 Join our Community Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EJrdn43jObx00BKnp444Rj

# ​📅 **Event Overview**

**Format:** 48-Hour Asynchronous Online Hackathon
**Team Size**: 1 to 4 Members per Squad
**Goal:** Build a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) addressing specific community tech challenges.

# 🛠️ The Challenge: Choose Your Problem Statement
Squads must select one of the following real-world challenges to solve. Your goal is to build a functional MVP with a clean User Interface.

> **1. The Developer Proof-of-Work Platform 🚀**
Many developers build great projects but lose them in scattered GitHub repositories. Build a centralized showcase directory where developers can host their deployed projects, tag their tech stack, and attach demo videos. Include filtering options (e.g., MERN, Web3, AI) for easy discovery.

>**2. The "Execution-First" Accountability Tracker 🔥**
Students often get stuck in "tutorial hell." Build a web dashboard that tracks a user's daily or weekly "build streak" based on actual project execution. The app should prompt users with "What did you code today?", visualize their consistency, and reward them with milestones.

>**3. The Skill-Based Teammate Matchmaker 🤝**
Finding the right teammates for hackathons or side projects is a major hurdle. Design a user-directory system where individuals can create profiles highlighting their specific skills (e.g., UI/UX, React, AI) and proficiency levels. Implement a search and filter mechanism to connect users.

> **4. The Crowdsourced Learning Vault 📚**
The internet is flooded with scattered resources. Build an organized, community-driven resource hub where users can submit and categorize high-quality links, tools, and guides. Include an upvote/downvote system so the best resources naturally rise to the top.

>**5. The Micro-Event & Submission Portal 🎯**
Small tech communities struggle to manage asynchronous events through chaotic group chats. Create a streamlined event dashboard displaying hackathon details, rules, and deadlines. It must feature a dedicated submission portal where teams can upload their final deliverables.

# 🎯 What You Need to Submit (The Deliverables)
To successfully complete the hackathon, your squad must submit the following three items:

 > **1. The Website MVP (Minimum Viable Product)**

**Build What You Can:** If you are a beginner, building just a clean, functional frontend MVP is completely fine. If you have the skills, you are highly encouraged to build the full-stack version (Frontend + Backend/Database)!

> **2. The Pitch Video (Max 10 Minutes)**

This is your final presentation! Record your screen and your voice.
**How to do it:** Walk us through your PPT first, and then give a live demo of your Website MVP.
**The Vibe:** Be confident! Explain your thought process, why you designed the UI a certain way, and how the code logic works.

# 📅 Buildathon 1.0: Official Timeline
**Phase 1: Registration & Concept Submission**
Date: 4th May
Duration: 24 Hours
Task: Register your team on Devfolio and start working on any problem statement given above.

**Phase 2: The 48-Hour Build Sprint**
Task: Start coding your MVP (Minimum Viable Product). This is the main development phase where you build your frontend/full-stack solution.
Submission: Keep your Deployed Website Link.

**Phase 3: Final Submission & Video Pitch**
Final Deliverables: 
1. Deployed Website Link. (In Project Links)
2. GitHub Repo URL. (In Project Links)
3. Final Video Demo (Max 10 Minutes):(YouTube link)

Important: The Devfolio submission portal will automatically close at 11:59 PM on 6th May.

**📅 Important Instructions for Participants:**

Strict Deadlines: Submissions after the round deadline will lead to automatic disqualification.

Communication: All shortlisting announcements will be made via the official Devlynix WhatsApp group and Devfolio notifications.

# 📊 Evaluation Criteria
Judges will evaluate your submissions out of 100 Points based on these 4 pillars:

**Problem-Solution Fit (25 Points):** How practical and realistic is your solution?
**UI/UX & Design (25 Points):** Is the layout user-friendly, clean, and adhering to the 'Silent Coder' aesthetic?
**Technical Logic (25 Points):** How functional is the code, or how clearly is the technical architecture defined?
**The Final Pitch (25 Points):** How well was the product explained and demonstrated in the video?

*Get ready to build. Good luck, Squads! Let's build something awesome. 🛠️🔥*

**Prizes, all of them non-monetary.** The event publishes six prize entries and every one of them carries a zero amount: Grand Prize (a shoutout on the organiser's LinkedIn page, a Certificate of Excellence and one-to-one portfolio mentorship), Runner-Up Squad (a community Wall of Fame place and a digital Certificate of Merit), Best UI/UX Award, Pure Coder Award, 2nd Runner Up, and a Certificate of Participation for a hundred entrants. There is no cash pool to record, which is why this record carries no `fundingInfo`.

**Announcement date not established.** The hosting platform publishes no date for when this listing went up, the organisers published no dated announcement that could be retrieved, and the first archive capture of the event's own pages post-dates registration opening. `postedAt` is therefore absent — the Standard's "unknown" — rather than a guess.
